**⭐ So the two Sestan men of house 2 both married a Defranceschi.** *Joannes Sestan took* **Sancta Alexandra**; *Antonius Sestan took* **Joanna**, *[out of Gračišće house 4, married 13 February 1843](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/).* *And at both baptisms the godfather is the same* **Franciscus Defranceschi**.

**⚠ And the register and the census disagree about this child.** *The 1826* status animarum, *read on 30 September, enters Joanna's eldest as* **Maria, born 8 October 1843, in house 3**. *The baptism register enters her* **born 7 November 1843 and baptised on the 11th, in house 2**. ***A month and a house apart, and both are doc.*** *The month figures were checked against each other on the same page — the* «8bris 8ᵃ» *of the row above and the* «9bris 11ᵃ» *of this one are written with plainly different numerals — so this is not a misreading here.* **The discrepancy is left standing and visible**, *because [this archive has already learnt that the census records baptism dates rather than births](/gologorica-line/), and a case where that rule does not close the gap is worth more as a question than as a patched date.*

> **«9bris 15 [1843] · [domus] 5 · TERESIA nata 14 hujus · Antonius Defranceschi · Francisca · Antonio Salamon et Maria soror · cives»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069118, folio 104.)*

**⭐ And a date made exact.** *The daughter of* **Antonius Defranceschi and Francisca** *has stood in this archive as* «Theresia Defranceschi, **ABT 1843**», *a tree estimate.* ***She was born 14 November 1843 and baptised on the 15th***, *at house* **5** — *the household that was house 6 in 1826, when Antonius was [the adopted nephew settled there](/gologorica-line/).*

**⚠ THE GODFATHER'S SURNAME READS «SALAMON» — AND THE TEST WAS RUN BEFORE THIS WAS PUBLISHED.**

*Four days ago this archive [withdrew a «Salman» lead on the Salomon maternal line](/corrections/) because the family turned out to be* **PALMAN** *and a patronymic proved it.* **So the word here was not written up until it had been set beside this scribe's own Palman.** *Petrus Milcetich writes* «Franciscus **Palman** sutor» *on folio 102, 28 April 1841, eleven folios earlier — and the two words, cut from the film at one magnification and put one above the other, are not the same word:*

| | Palman, 1841 | Salamon, 1843 |
|---|---|---|
| **initial** | *a tall closed majuscule bowl, the same form as his* **B** *in* «Brussich» | *a small low pointed stroke with no bowl* |
| **body** | *a · l · m · a · n* | *a · l · **a** · m · **o** · n* |
| **letters** | six | seven |

***The medial «a» between the l and the m is the clincher: Palman has nothing there.*** **The 1843 word is not Palman.**

**What that does and does not establish.** *It establishes that a man surnamed* **Salamon** *— not Palman — stood godfather to a Defranceschi child at Gologorica on 15 November 1843, entered* **civis**, *with* «**Maria soror**» *beside him, which makes him a household rather than a stray name.* **It does not establish a connection to [Francisca Salomon's family](/maternal/salomon/).** *That would need this Antonio Salamon tied to Gračišće, four kilometres away, and nothing here does it.* ***This is a lead, and it is the first one on the Salomon line that has survived its own test.*** *[The worklist carries what would turn it into a line](/worklist/).*

sorella.heading: «Franciscus Defranceschi e Maria sorella» — the register names a sister
sorella.lead: **The surname that was absent for ten folios is now on nearly every page**, *and almost always in the godparent column.* *Through 1844 and 1845* **Franciscus**, **Matthea** *and* **Francisca Defranceschi** *stand at the Gologorica font for one neighbour's child after another — and one entry describes a relationship instead of just listing two names.*
paras:
> **«Vitus Ancich · Maria nata Udovicich · FRANCISCUS DEFRANCESCHI e MARIA SORELLA · cives»**

*(doc — Gologorica baptisms, DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069119, folio 105, 1844.)*

***Sorella*** *— Italian for sister, dropped into a Latin entry.* **So there is a Maria Defranceschi who is the sister of the Franciscus Defranceschi who keeps appearing**, *and the pair are entered* **cives**, *the standing this household has carried since 1810.* *The same construction turns up a second time on this run of folios, at [Teresia Defranceschi's baptism](/person/teresia-defranceschi-1843/), where the godparents are* «Antonio Salamon et **Maria soror**» — ***a different Maria and a different brother***, *and the two should not be confused.*

**Who they are, as an inference and marked as one.** *The only Franciscus-and-Maria pair of adult Defranceschi siblings this archive can name at Gologorica in 1844 is* **Franciscus Xaverius Joseph** *(born 19 February 1816, died 4 January 1893) and* **[Maria Aloysia](/person/maria-defranceschi-1811/)** *(born 14 August 1811, died 1897)* — ***Carlo De Franceschi's own brother and sister***, *twenty-eight and thirty-three that year, both of the* civis *household.* **(inf.)**

**⚠ And the weakness of that inference, stated rather than buried.** *«The only pair this archive can name» is not «the only pair».* **These very pages have just produced three grown Defranceschi women the pedigree does not contain** — *[Sancta Alexandra](/who/sancta-alexandra-defranceschi-sestan/), [Matthea](/who/matthea-defranceschi/) and a Clementina who cannot be assigned to either of the two the family had.* *A village whose register knows Defranceschi the archive does not is a village where «the only known pair» proves very little.* **The identification is offered, not asserted, and no page is rewritten on it.**

**⭐ Meanwhile the women of house 2 keep bearing.** **Sancta Alexandra's third child** *—* «**Josephus** natus hodie», ***21 March 1844***, *house 2, godfather the locksmith Francesco Marciolin again (M01069119, folio 105).* *And* **Joanna's second** *—* «**Antonia** nata heri», ***born 16 July 1845, baptised the 17th***, *house 2 (M01069120, folio 106).*

**⭐ Which sharpens yesterday's doubt instead of confirming it.** *This archive recorded that the 1826* status animarum *and the baptism register disagree by a month about Joanna's eldest.* **They agree exactly about her second**: *the census gives Antonia born* **16 July 1845**; *the register gives her born the day before her baptism of* **17 July 1845**. ***So the census is not generally unreliable on this family, and the gap over Maria is an anomaly in one entry rather than a property of the source.*** *It stays open, and it is now a sharper question than it was.*

**⭐ And a date confirmed to the day.** **Maria Defranceschi**, *daughter of* **Antonius and Francisca** *of house 5, is entered* «**Maria** nata **18 hujus**», *baptised 20 July 1845 (M01069120, folio 106).* *The tree already had* **18 July 1845**. **Verification, not discovery, and the archive says so** — *but a tree date with a register behind it is a different thing from a tree date without one.* *Her mother is written* «**Francisca n. Defranceschi**» *once more, the* n. *for* nata *that [settled her as a marriage inside the name](/gologorica-line/).*

etsoror.heading: «et soror Adelaidis» — the register places a woman the pedigree could not
etsoror.lead: **The formula that turned up in 1844 as «e Maria sorella» turns up again in 1847, and this time both names are ones this archive already holds.** *It does something a godparent entry very rarely does:* ***it puts a person into a family.***
paras:
> **«Jacobus Cocolet · Maria nata Petorin · MAXIMILIANUS DEFRANCESCHI ET SOROR ADELAIDIS · cives»**

*21 October 1847, house 7. (doc — Gologorica baptisms, DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069122, folio 108.)*

**⭐ [Adelaidis Defranceschi](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/) has stood in this roster as «tree-derived, no register read for this person here», line* **unplaced**. *She is now placed.* *Her brother* **Maximilianus** *is* **Maximilianus Antonius Josephus**, *born 8 January 1828 and baptised the 9th — [the entry this archive found four days ago](/gologorica-line/) — son of* **Josephus Defranceschi and Lambertina née Peschle**. *So Adelaidis is their daughter too, and the* **«Maria Adelgidis»** *the 1826* status animarum *lists sixth among their ten children is her.*

**And the register confirms it independently of the census**, *which matters: the census list and the family tree are two readings of the same household, and until now nothing outside them said these two were siblings.* **A godparent cell written twenty-one years later, by a different priest, says it in three words.**

**⚠ Which raises a question this archive is not closing.** *The pedigree gives Josephus and Lambertina a daughter* **Anastasia, born 8 December 1824**; *the 1826 census gives them a daughter* **Maria Adelgidis** *and no Anastasia; the roster carries* **Adelaidis, born 1824**, *as a separate and unplaced person.* ***Three names, one birth year, and possibly one child.*** *[The worklist holds it](/worklist/). Nothing is merged on a suspicion, and no id is moved.*

**It also settles how to read the 1844 entry.** *«[Franciscus Defranceschi e Maria sorella](/gologorica-line/)» was offered as an inference about Carlo's brother and sister, with its weakness published beside it.* **This entry shows the register using exactly that formula for exactly that household** — *two of the same ten children, named as brother and sister, entered* cives. *The inference is not proved by it, but it is no longer a guess about a form of words.*

> **«Januarii 23 · [domus] 5 · LEONARDUS natus heri · † 20.XII.1917»**

*of* «**Antonius Defranceschi**» *and* «**Francisca nata Defranceschi**». *(doc — same frame, folio 108.)*

**⭐ A birth and a death, seventy years apart, on one line.** *This archive held* **Leonardus Defranceschi, 1847–1917**, *off the family tree with an empty note. The register gives the day —* ***born 22 January 1847, baptised the 23rd*** *— and a twentieth-century hand has come back to the page and written his death into the margin:* **20 December 1917**. *Both years are confirmed and both are now exact.* **Verification, and the archive says so.**

**⭐ And the women of house 2 are still bearing.** **Sancta Alexandra's fourth child** *—* «**Francisca** nata hodie», ***7 February 1846*** *— and two more for* **Joanna**, *whose godmother in 1846 is* «**Lucia Defranceschi**». *This archive holds a* **Lucia Defranceschi born 1820 at Gračišće** *with an empty note, twenty-six that year.* **(inf, and no page is rewritten on it.)**

**⭐ Which makes a cohort, and it points at one parish.** *Three Defranceschi women of nearly the same age are at Gologorica in the 1840s and all three came out of* **Gračišće**: *[Joanna](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/), born 1818,* «Ex Parochia Gallignanæ sub N.º **4**»; *[Francisca](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1819/), born 1819,* «sub N.º **5**»; *and Lucia, born 1820, if she is the Lucia of this roster.* ***Gračišće house 5 is the direct line's own second generation.*** **The register that would name their fathers is on ZM34K-216, the one reel of this set the family does not hold, and [getting it is the archive's first errand](/errands/).**

rosa1848.heading: The register gives a child back her name, and takes fifty-one years off a blank
rosa1848.lead: **The family tree gave Antonius and Francisca a daughter «Joanna, born 9 June 1848», with no death.** *The baptism register of that week gives them a daughter too — and she is not called Joanna, she was not born on the 9th, and her death is written on the same line.*
paras:
> **«Junii 8ᵃ · [domus] 5 · ROSA nata heri · † 10/12 99»**

*of* «**Antonius Defranceschi**» *and* «**Francisca nata Defranceschi**»; *godparents* «Giovanni L— et **ADELINA DEFRANCESCHI**», *entered* **cives**. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069123, folio 109.)*

**One child, not two.** *A mother cannot bear children on the 7th and the 9th of one June; no second entry stands anywhere near it; the parents, the house and the week are the same.* ***So the tree's «Joanna, 9 June» and the register's «Rosa, nata heri» on the 8th are one girl***, *and the register is the document.* **[The correction is published](/corrections/)** *and her pid is kept —* `joanna-defranceschi-1848` *will read* «joanna» *for ever, because [a moved id is a dead URL](/method/). Only its id remembers the error.*

**⭐ And a later hand closed her life on the same line.** **«† 10/12 99»** — ***Rosa Defranceschi died 10 December 1899, aged fifty-one***, *where this archive had no death year at all.* *She is the fourth person on these few folios whose death a twentieth-century register keeper came back and wrote into a page sixty or seventy years old; the others are [Leonardus (1917)](/who/leonardus-defranceschi/), her nephew-by-marriage Antonius Sestan (1923) and a Gasparich of 1830 (1898).* **Somebody worked through this book closing lives, and the archive has been reading it as if it only recorded births.**

**A new given name, and a tempting one.** *Her godmother is* **«Adelina Defranceschi»**, *entered* **civis** *— written large and unambiguous.* *This archive now knows an* **[Adelaidis](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/)** *of the same household, placed four folios earlier as* «Maximilianus Defranceschi **et soror Adelaidis**», *and* **Adelina** *is the ordinary Italian diminutive of Adelaide.* **It is not claimed.** *[Worklist 175](/worklist/) already holds three names round one 1824 birth — Anastasia, Maria Adelgidis, Adelaidis — and a fourth is a reason to go and read the December 1824 folios, not a reason to guess.*

**⭐ And Sancta Alexandra's fifth child.** «**Antonius** natus **heri**», *baptised 27 March 1848, house* **2**, *godparents* «**Antonius Defranceschi** et Teresia Udovicich» — *and on his line too,* **«† 27.VIII.1923»**. ***Five children documented in eight years***, *for a woman this archive held [with an empty note and no husband](/who/sancta-alexandra-defranceschi-sestan/) at the start of the day.*

**⚠ How the day was read, because it decided the correction.** *The baptism is* «Junii **8**ᵃ»; *the row beneath it is* «Julii **9**ᵃ». *The two numerals were cut from the film in one crop and compared:* **the 8 is a double loop, the 9 a single loop with a descender.** *That is [the rule this archive learnt at eight o'clock this morning](/corrections/) after publishing a 73 as a 75 — crop past the cell, not to it — applied the same day to a reading that changes a published name.*

**✔ And the margins were gone back over the same afternoon, which is how this archive found out what they are worth.** *Every Defranceschi baptism in the first hundred folios was re-cropped and read for its margin alone.* **Two of six carry one, and both were already known** — *Franciscus Xaverius († 4 January 1893) and Maximilianus Antonius († 6 August 1910).* ***No new dates.***

**⚠ But the count is the point.** *On folio 73 one entry of three carries a dagger; on folio 89, one of five.* ***The later keeper's sweep through this book is partial***, *so* **a blank margin is not evidence that anybody lived**. *That lands straight on an open question: [the Clementina of 1821](/person/clementina-defranceschi-1821/) has no dagger, and the inference that she died young is neither supported nor refuted by the silence. [The burial register](/worklist/) is still the only thing that settles her.*

censustest.heading: One household, two sources, and the first real test of the 1826 census
censustest.lead: **This archive leans hard on the 1826 *status animarum*.** *It gave Carlo's household, his mother's birthday, the adoption in house 6, and sixty maiden surnames of the village. Until today nothing had checked it against a second document for the same family, entry by entry.* **Joanna née Defranceschi's children are that check, because the baptism register has now given all five.**
paras:
| child | the 1826 *status animarum* | the baptism register | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Maria** | born **8 October 1843** | born **7 November 1843**, bapt. the 11th | ***a month apart*** |
| **Antonia** | born **16 July 1845** | born **16 July 1845**, bapt. the 17th | **exact** |
| **Catharina** | *— not listed —* | born **1 October 1846**, bapt. the 2nd | ***the census omits her*** |
| **Antonius** | born **4 June 1849** | born and baptised **4 June 1849** | **exact** |
| **Joannes** | born **6 June 1852** | born **6 June 1851**, bapt. the 7th | ***a year apart*** |

*(doc both ways — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**: *census M01069323; register M01069118, M01069120, M01069121, M01069124, M01069126.)*

**⭐ What the table says about the census is specific, and it is better news than a flat verdict.** ***The day is right every single time.*** *Where the two sources disagree they disagree on the* **month** *or the* **year**, *never on the day of the month — which is the signature of a figure miscopied when the household was written up, not of a source that is guessing.* **So a census date is good evidence for the day and weaker evidence for the month and year**, *and anyone using one should say which part they are leaning on.*

**⚠ And it omits a child.** **Catharina**, *born 1 October 1846, is in the register and not in the census.* *She may have died before 1826's book was brought up to date for this household, or been missed.* ***Either way the census's list of a family's children is a floor, not a ceiling***, *and this archive has been reading such lists as complete.*

> **«Junii 7ᵃ · [domus] 3 · JOANNES natus heri · † 27/2 1935»**

*of* «**Antonius Sestan**» *and* «**Joanna nata Defranceschi**», *godparents* «Joannes Ivich et **Francisca Defranceschi**». *(doc — M01069126, folio 112.)*

**⭐ Eighty-four years after his baptism somebody came back to this page and closed him.** *It is the latest of [the marginal deaths](/gologorica-line/) this book carries, and the fourth in which a Defranceschi or a child of one is the subject.*

**⭐ And another «about» became a day.** **Antonia Defranceschi**, *daughter of* **Antonius and Francisca** *of house 5, has stood in this archive as* «ABT 1849». *The register enters her* «**Antonia** nata **heri**» *on* **24 December 1849** — ***born 23 December 1849***. *(doc — M01069124, folio 110.)* *Her brother* **Antonius, born 4 June 1849 at house 2**, *is the Sestan child above and not to be confused with her.*

**And 1850 is a clean nil.** *Folio 111 (M01069125) carries fourteen baptisms and* **not one Defranceschi in any column** — *the first whole year of this walk with no sighting at all. It is recorded because [a nil names the exact terms tried](/method/), and a year of silence in a village where the name stood at four fonts the year before is itself worth knowing.*

enrico1852.heading: Enrico stands at the font with his sister, and two German names turn up in the Peschle house
enrico1852.lead: **The man whose baptism opened this day's work turns up in it again, twenty-two years older.** *On 13 March 1852 the godparents of Joannes Junco's child are* **«Enrico Defranceschi et soror Adelaidis»**, *entered* **cives**.
paras: **⭐ That is [Enrichus Jacobus](/who/henricus-jacobus-defranceschi/), born 11 March 1830 — two days past his twenty-second birthday.** *This archive knew him as a name on the family tree with a death at Trieste in 1906 and nothing in between.* ***It now has him alive at Gologorica, of age, and chosen to stand at its font.*** *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069127, folio 113.)*

**And the register calls him ENRICO.** *The Italian form, after* «Enrichus» *in 1830 and* «Enrichus» *in the 1826 census.* ***Three hands, three times, and not one of them writes the H this archive carries.***

**⭐ It is also the third time the book names this household's siblings by the same formula.** *«Franciscus Defranceschi* **e Maria sorella**» *in 1844, «Maximilianus Defranceschi* **et soror Adelaidis**» *in 1847, and now «Enrico Defranceschi* **et soror Adelaidis**» *in 1852.* **[Adelaidis](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/) is named as a sister twice, by two different brothers** — *which is as firm as a godparent column gets, and it is what moved her from «unplaced» into Josephus and Lambertina's house.*

> **«Julii 28 · [domus] 2 · CONRADUS, JOSEPHUS ac VICTORIUS natus 20 hujus · Albertus Peschle, D.r Medicinæ, Civis · Victoria nata Calligarich · Cost. SCHROTT, Carolina WALSER · cives»**

*(doc — M01069128, folio 114.)*

**This household the archive already had**, *and it says so:* **Dr Albertus Peschle**, *physician, head of Gologorica house 2 in the 1826* status animarum, *with* **Victoria née Calligarich** *and their son* **Conradus Josephus Victorius, born 20 July 1853** — *[all of it on the married-in page](/married-in/) since the census was walked.* **Verification, not discovery.** *What is new is small and specific: the* **baptism** *date, 28 July, and the* **godparents**.

**⚠ And the godparents are the reason this entry is worth a paragraph.** **«Cost. Schrott»** *and* **«Carolina Walser»** — ***two unmistakably German surnames standing at an Istrian font***, *chosen by a Peschle.* *[Worklist 170](/worklist/) asks whether the Peschle are a German family who arrived on the Kvarner rather than a Kvarner family, on the strength of one godmother* «ex Silesia» *in 1822 and the fact that* **Peschel**, **Peschke** *and* **Pöschl** *are ordinary German names.* **This does not answer it. It is the second time the question has been raised by the company a Peschle keeps, and the first time by a household rather than a single visitor.**

**⚠ What it is NOT.** *Schrott and Walser are German or Austrian; they are not* **Silesian** *in particular, and neither name is tied here to any place.* *A doctor of medicine in Habsburg Istria moved in a German-speaking professional world as a matter of course.* ***Nothing here says where his family came from***, *and the archive is recording two names and a question, not a conclusion.*

**⭐ And Joanna's sixth child, with the census out by two years this time.** *«Januarii 31 · [domus] 3 ·* **FRANCISCUS** *natus hodie», of* «Antonius Sestan» *and* «Joanna nata Defranceschi» *— born and baptised* **31 January 1853**. *The 1826* status animarum *gives him* **31 January 1855**. ***The day and the month agree exactly and the year is two out***, *which is the third time this household's census dates have failed in precisely that shape. [The pattern is set out in full here](/gologorica-line/).*
**And a sixth visitation.** *«Vidi. Petinae die 16 Januarii 1854» —* **Coverlizza, Decanus**, *inspecting at Pićan for the sixth recorded year running. [Worklist 169](/worklist/) carries them all.*

deathbook.heading: Three collisions, one book, and the case for opening the register of the dead
deathbook.lead: **This archive now holds three unresolved contradictions about when a Defranceschi of Gologorica died — and all three are closed by the same ninety-one frames, which sit on the reel the family already owns and have barely been opened.**
paras:
| person | one source says | the other says | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Clementina Maria](/person/clementina-maria-defranceschi-1822/)**, b. 1822 | **1840** *(this archive)* | **1870** *(the tree)* | ***thirty years*** |
| **[Josephus Lambertus](/who/josephus-lambertus-defranceschi/)**, b. 1808 | **1857** *(this archive)* | **1878** *(the tree)* | ***twenty-one years*** |
| **[Antonius](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1853/)**, b. 1855 | **1913** *(the register's own margin)* | **1918** *(the tree)* | ***five years*** |

**A death year is usually the better-evidenced of a person's two dates**, *so a gap this wide normally means one side is describing* **a different person of the same name in the same parish** *— which in a one-name study is not an edge case but the ordinary condition.* ***Three of them in one family is a pattern, and the pattern names its own remedy.***

**⚠ And note what the third one does to a comfortable assumption.** *Antonius's 1913 comes from the* **margin of his own baptism entry**, *written by a later keeper sixty years after the event; the 1918 comes from a family tree.* **Both are second-hand to the death.** *This archive spent an hour this afternoon learning to read those margins and must not now treat them as a burial register. [They are partial, and a blank one is not evidence of life](/gologorica-line/); a dated one is still hearsay beside the entry made on the day.*

**⭐ The book that answers all three.** **Gologorica deaths, 1784–1880 — DAPA ZM34K-214, frames M01069224 to M01069314, ninety-one of them.** *It covers every year the three disputes fall in except Antonius's 1913 or 1918, which the [1894 *status animarum*](/worklist/) on the same reel reaches instead.* ***About two per cent of it has ever been read.***

**It would also answer things nobody has asked it yet.** *Whether [the Clementina of 1821](/person/clementina-defranceschi-1821/) died a child, which is the hinge of [the reused-name argument](/gologorica-line/); when [Matthea](/who/matthea-defranceschi/) and [Adelaidis](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/) died; and whether the Defranceschi women who came out of Gračišće were buried at Gologorica under their maiden name or their husbands'.* **Every one of those is a blank on a page a reader can already reach.**

**This section is not a finding. It is a decision written down**, *so that the next session does not have to rediscover the argument for it:* ***when the baptism book is finished, the death book is next, and it is walked rather than sampled.***

census2.heading: The census is now short by two children, and a priest from Krbune walks in
census2.lead: **Folios 117 to 119 finish Joanna née Defranceschi's family in the baptism register, and the comparison with the 1826 *status animarum* gets worse in one way and better in another.**
paras:
| child | the 1826 *status animarum* | the baptism register | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maria | 8 October 1843 | **7 November 1843** | *a month* |
| Antonia | 16 July 1845 | **16 July 1845** | **exact** |
| **Catharina** | *— not listed —* | **1 October 1846** | ***omitted*** |
| Antonius | 4 June 1849 | **4 June 1849** | **exact** |
| Joannes | 6 June 1852 | **6 June 1851** | *a year* |
| Franciscus | 31 January 1855 | **31 January 1853** | *two years* |
| **Francisca** | *— not listed —* | **30 May 1856** | ***omitted*** |
| Josephus | 2 February 1858 | **2 February 1858** | **exact** |

**⭐ Three of the eight are exact, and the day of the month is right in all eight.** *That holds: where the two sources differ they differ on the month or the year and never on the day.* ***But the census is short by two whole children***, *not one — Catharina of 1846 and Francisca of 1856, both baptised at Gologorica, both absent from the household page.* **A census list of a family's children is a floor, and this archive has been reading such lists as ceilings.**

**⭐ And Sancta Alexandra's seventh.** *«Maij 8ᵃ · [domus]* **9** *·* **FRANCISCUS** *natus* **6 Maij**», *1857, of* «Joannes Sestan» *and* «Sancta nata Defranceschi» *— with* **«† 18/1 1932»** *in the margin. (doc — M01069132, folio 118.)* ***Seven children between 1840 and 1857***, *for a woman who had an empty note this morning.*

> **«1858 Februarii 1ᵃ · [domus] 55 · FRANCISCUS P— Ad.r PAR. CHERBUNIS»**

*(doc — M01069133, folio 119.)*

**⭐ A priest of KRBUNE comes to Gologorica to baptise.** *The* baptizans *column, which has read* «Petrus Milcetich, Parochus» *for twenty-three years, names for one entry* **the administrator of the parish of Cherbune** — ***Krbune***. *[Worklist 168](/worklist/) was raised on 1 October because* **«Archipresbiter GRACH of Cherbune»** *stood godfather to a Defranceschi child in 1785, and the archive could find only* **one** *collection for the place against thirty-two for Gračišće.*

**What this adds is small and solid:** ***Krbune was a parish in its own right with its own administrator in 1858***, *and its clergy and Gologorica's covered for one another.* **A parish that lends a priest keeps a register**, *and the one bound volume the atlas lists — births, deaths and marriages 1803–1870 — is the right book and not a fragment of somebody else's.*

**⚠ The priest's own surname is not settled** *and is not published here.* *It reads as* **Pasnich**, **Papich** *or* **Bascich** *and has not been set against the same hand writing any of those elsewhere.* *[A hand is only legible against itself](/method/), and the office and the parish — which are both plain — carry the finding without it.*

**And the deanery keeps coming.** *«Vidi. Petinae»* **15 January 1857**, **8 January 1858**, **7 January 1859** — *all* **Coverlizza, Decanus**. ***Nine consecutive Januaries*** *(with one May), which makes the visitation annual and its protocols a series rather than a scattering. [Worklist 169](/worklist/) carries them.*

anselmus.heading: A Peschle stands godfather by proxy, and the next generation opens at house 7
anselmus.lead: **Folio 121 is where this book turns a corner.** *For thirty years the Defranceschi in it have been godparents and wives; now* **Franciscus Defranceschi, civis**, *is a father, at* **house 7** — *the house his own father Josephus held in the 1826 census — and the man he asks to stand for his daughter is a* **Peschle**.*
paras:
> **«1860. 9bris 4ᵃ · [domus] 7 · ANNA-MARIA FRANCISCA nata 28 8bris · Franciscus Defranceschi, civis · Clotildis Ortis · ANSELMUS PESCHLE … per procuratorem · Beatrice Ortis · cives»**

*with* **«† Tergesti 22-6-1941»** *added above the entry by a later hand, and the midwife* «Catharina Cattenar». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069135, folio 121.)*

**The child this archive already had.** *[Anna Maria Francisca Defranceschi](/who/anna-maria-francisca-defranceschi/) was [corrected on 13 September](/corrections/) from a roster year of «1880» to* **born at Gologorica 28 October 1860, died at Trieste 22 June 1941** — *and the register agrees with both, to the day.* **Verification, and said so.** *What is new is the* **baptism** *(4 November), the* **house** *(7), the midwife, and the godparents.*

**⭐ ANSELMUS PESCHLE, and he was not there.** *The godfather is entered* **«per procuratorem»** — *by proxy, the formula used when the chosen godparent cannot come and a stand-in holds the child for him.* ***So Franciscus Defranceschi wanted a Peschle at his daughter's font badly enough to have one in absentia.***

**This archive has never met an Anselmus Peschle.** *It knows* **[Lambertina née Peschle](/who/lambertina-defranceschi-peschle/)**, *Carlo's mother, married into this house in 1807; it knows* **Amalia Peschle «ex Silesia»**, *godmother in 1822; it knows* **Dr Albertus Peschle**, *physician of house 2, [whose own child's godparents were the German-named Schrott and Walser](/gologorica-line/). Anselmus is the fourth.*

**⚠ What that is worth, stated carefully.** *Four Peschle across fifty years at one Istrian village, three of them standing at Defranceschi or Peschle fonts, one of them* «ex Silesia», *one a doctor of medicine, and this one* ***summoned from somewhere else by proxy***. **That is a family with reach, and it is not yet a family with an origin.** *[Worklist 170](/worklist/) asks whether they are German-Silesian who arrived on the Kvarner rather than a Kvarner family;* ***nothing here answers it***, *and a proxy godfather tells you he was away without telling you where.*

**⭐ And the house number is the quiet part.** *The baptisms of this family through the 1840s were at houses* **5**, **6**, **8** *and* **9**; *this one is at* **7** — *the number the 1826* status animarum *gives Josephus Defranceschi's household, Carlo's own.* ***The son is baptising his children in his father's house.*** *(Given [what this archive has learnt about the book's two numberings](/gologorica-line/), that is offered as the plain reading of a single figure and not as a proof of tenure.)*

**Meanwhile the two Sestan households finish their families.** **Sancta Alexandra's eighth child** — «**Catharina** nata **heri**», *24 June 1859, house 9* — *and* **Joanna's ninth**, *born 15 September 1859 at house 3, with* **Francisca Defranceschi** *godmother again.* ***Between them the two Defranceschi daughters of house 2 bore fifteen children that this register names***, *where the archive this morning had none at all.*

handover1862.heading: The page where a parish priest stops writing, and a son is called «possessor»
handover1862.lead: **Folio 123 does something no other page in this book does: it shows a man dying.** *Not in an entry — the deaths are not kept here — but in the* baptizans *column, which runs* «Petrus Milcetich, Parochus» *for twenty-seven years and then simply stops.*
paras:
| 1862 | baptised by |
|---|---|
| 3 January – **13 March** | **Petrus Milcetich, Parochus** |
| **13 April** onward | **Blasius Zwölber, Administrator** |

**⭐ The 1826 *status animarum* says Milcetich died on 22 March 1862**, *aged 58 years 2 months 15 days, [«mortuus et sepultus Gollogoricæ»](/gologorica-line/).* ***The register brackets that date without naming it*** — *his last signature is nine days before it and his successor's first is three weeks after.* **Two independent books, one man, and they agree.** *After a day spent finding places where [the census and this register disagree](/gologorica-line/), it is worth recording a place where they do not.*

**Blasius Zwölber is one of the eight** *the parish-house page names — born 1 February 1822* «e Zuckfeld», *dead 22 May 1879 — so for once the roll of priests and the hand in the book are the same list. [They have not always been](/gologorica-line/).*

> **«1862 Aprilis 27 · [domus] 7 · VICTOR JOSEPHUS natus 22 Aprilis · Franciscus Xav. Defranceschi, POSSESSOR · Clotildis Ortis · Natalis Stefanovich, MARIA DEFRANCESCHI · cives»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069137, folio 123.)*

**⭐ Victor Josephus, the second child of this marriage to be found in a week.** *The pedigree had him as* «1862»; *he was* ***born 22 April 1862 and baptised on the 27th***, *at* **house 7** *— the same house as [his sister Anna Maria Francisca eighteen months earlier](/gologorica-line/).*

**⭐ And his father has a new word.** *Through the 1840s and 1850s the Defranceschi of this book are* **civis**. *Here Franciscus Xaverius is* **«possessor»** — ***a holder of property***, *written in the* conditio *slot where the neighbours get* «agricola». *It is the first time the register distinguishes this family by what it owns rather than by its standing.* **⚠ One word on one line is not an estate**, *and no page is rewritten on it; it is recorded because [the 1820 cadastre](/gologorica-line/) is already on the archive's list and this is the kind of word that cadastre would answer.*

**The godmother is Maria Defranceschi** — *the same name that stood as* «Maria sorella» *to Franciscus in 1844. If that identification holds she is [Maria Aloysia](/person/maria-defranceschi-1811/), fifty-one here, standing for her brother's son.* **(inf, and still inference.)**

**⭐ And Sancta Alexandra's ninth.** *«1862 Julii 8 · [domus]* **9** *·* **ELISABETHA** *nata* **7 Julii 1862**», *of* «**Joannes Sestan, POSSIDENS**» *and* «Sancta n. Defranceschi». ***Nine children, 1840 to 1862.*** *And her husband too has changed word:* **sutor**, *then* **lapicida**, *then* **agricola**, *then* **textor**, *and now* **possidens**. **No trade is taken from this book for that man** — *[it has given four and they do not agree](/who/sancta-alexandra-defranceschi-sestan/)* — *but a man entered* possidens *in 1862 is not the man entered* sutor *in 1840, and the drift is one way.*

**⚠ And a byname for the Grah, which [worklist 168](/worklist/) should have.** *Two rows below Victor's, the mother and a godmother are both entered* **«Grah»** *with* **«Missan»** *written beneath the surname —* «Mariana Grah / Missan» *and* «Cathar. Grah / missan». ***Whether Missan is a byname in the manner of [«Flegar alias Sidre»](/gologorica-line/) or a place has not been settled here***, *and it is not claimed as either. It is recorded because the Grah are [the family behind the Krbune item](/worklist/) and a second word attached to a common surname is exactly what makes one findable.*

duplicates.heading: A second set of these registers left the parish every year
duplicates.lead: **The strip this archive had been cropping off the bottom of every page turned out to hold the most useful thing on the film.** *Ruled across the foot of folio 98, beneath the last baptism of 1835:*
paras:
> **«Quae copiae collationatae anni 1835 concordant cum hoc originali libro. Ex officio Decanatus, Petinae die 7 Maij 1836.»** — *signed,* **Decanus**

*«Which collated copies of the year 1835 agree with this original book. By office of the Deanery, at Pićan, 7 May 1836.»* *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069111, folio 98.)*

**⭐ Read it carefully, because it is a statement about a document that is not in the picture.** *The parish* **made a copy** *of each year's entries. The dean* **collated** *that copy against this original and certified that the two agreed.* ***So a second, certified set of these registers went out of Gologorica every year, and this film holds the one that stayed.***

**This is the ordinary Habsburg practice and this archive had not registered that it applied here.** *A parish kept the original; a* **duplicate** *went up to the deanery, and from the deanery to the diocese. Where the originals have been lost, burnt or are closed, the duplicates are what genealogists read.* **Here the originals survive — so the duplicates are not a rescue. They are something better: an independent witness.**

**⭐ WHAT IT IS WORTH TO THIS ARCHIVE, CONCRETELY.**

1. **The reel the family does not hold.** *[Gračišće house 5 and house 4](/gologorica-line/) — where [Francisca](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1819/), [Joanna](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/) and probably [Lucia](/who/lucia-defranceschi/) were born — are on* **ZM34K-216**, *and getting it is [the archive's first errand](/errands/).* ***If Gračišće's parish also sent annual copies to the same deanery, there is a second route to the same entries.***
2. **The three death-year collisions.** *[A duplicate death register](/gologorica-line/) is a second chance at the same burials.*
3. **Checking the book against itself.** *Where this register disagrees with the 1826 census — [and it does, on five of Joanna's eight children](/gologorica-line/) — a contemporary certified copy is an independent third reading.*

**⚠ AND THE CAUTIONS, because this is a lead and not a holding.** *Nothing here says the duplicates* **survive**; *nothing says* **where** *they went after the deanery; and a certificate of 1836 proves the practice for one year at one parish, not for every year or every parish.* ***This archive has not looked for them and is not claiming they exist.*** *What it now knows is that they were made — which is the difference between a search with a target and a search without one.* [Worklist 178](/worklist/) *carries it.*

**⚠ And a correction that comes with it.** *Earlier today this archive wrote that the deanery was* **«still seated at Pićan»** *fifty years after its diocese was suppressed, on the strength of five certificates reading* «Vidi. **Petinae**». *A sixth, of* **15 March 1849**, *reads* **«Vidi. Pizinae»** — ***Pazin***, *a different town, the letter unmistakable beside the others.* **Both forms are in the book.** *So the dean signed at Pićan in the 1830s and 40s and at Pazin in 1849, and [«the deanery's own seat» was a claim the evidence did not carry](/corrections/). The named deans and the dates stand; the address does not.*

caesar.heading: A Caesar Peschle is born at Gologorica, and an army doctor stops being a stranger
caesar.lead: **This archive has carried a man it could not place for weeks.** *Fifty-one hits on Hungaricana, almost all of them* **Dr Cäsar Peschle**, *medical officer of the* **K. K. Landwehr**, *commissioned 1 August 1895, Assistenzarzt with the 5th and 23rd Regiments, attached to the Landsturm district of Gorizia and still on the lists in 1918.* ***Twenty-three years of a career, and the Peschle page said under it: «Nothing joins him to Lambertina.»***
paras:
> **«1864 Octobris 9 · [domus] 4 · REMIGIUS CÆSAR natus 1 Oct. · Albertus Peschle, Doctor medicinæ · Victoria nata Calligarich · Luigi De Franceschi, Celestina V.da Calligarich · industriante»**

*midwife* «Joanna Crismanich». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069140, folio 126.)*

**⭐ A Caesar Peschle, born at Gologorica on 1 October 1864, to a doctor of medicine.** *Four things agree with the man on the army lists at once: the* **surname**, *the* **given name** *— uncommon enough to be worth something —* *the* **profession in the household**, *and the* **age**: *a man born in October 1864 is* ***just under thirty-one*** *when that commission is granted in August 1895, which is exactly when an* Assistenzarzt *is commissioned after his training.*

**⚠ It is an inference and it is written as one.** *The Hungaricana entries are army lists; they give rank, regiment and date and not a birthplace.* ***Nothing in either record names the other.*** *What this archive now has is a Gologorica birth that fits an Austrian career at four points, where before it had a career attached to nothing.* **(inf.)** *[The Peschle page carries it](/married-in/peschle/), and so does the caution.*

**And it matters because of where he was.** *The Peschle page has long noted that Cäsar Peschle's Landsturm district was* **Gorizia** *— and that* **Gorizia is where Carlo De Franceschi was sent to the seminary**. *That was recorded as a coincidence of place and not evidence.* ***It is still not evidence. But a coincidence between two strangers is worth less than a coincidence between a man and his mother's family's village***, *and this entry is what moves it from the first kind to the second.*

**⭐ And the godfather is a Defranceschi, in Italian.** **«Luigi De Franceschi»** *— Luigi is Aloysius.* *[Aloysius Defranceschi](/who/aloysius-defranceschi/), born 8 May 1832 at Volosca and dead in 1870 — [the brother whose birthplace this archive corrected from «Polonia» to «Volosca»](/gologorica-line/) — was thirty-two in 1864.* **(inf.)** *The conditio reads* **«industriante»**, *a tradesman — a word new to this register.*

**⭐ Meanwhile the house-7 family adds another daughter.** *«1863 Decemb. 20 · [domus]* **7** *·* **AMALIA LAMBERTINA** *nata* **14 Dic. 1863**», *of* «Franciscus X. Defranceschi, **poss.**» *and* «Clotilde n. Ortis»; *godparents* **Raimondo** *and* **Marietta Baxa**, *cives.* *(doc — M01069139, folio 125.)* **The pedigree already had 14 December 1863** *— from the 1894 census —* ***and the register agrees to the day.*** *Verification, and the baptism, the house and the godparents are new. **Her second name is her grandmother's**: Lambertina née Peschle, who married into this house in 1807.*

**⚠ And a reading corrected before it was published.** *At first look the figure read* **19 December**. *Cut past the cell and enlarged, the second digit is an open-topped* **4** *with no loop — against the closed-loop* **9** *of the entry number* «19» *on the same line.* ***14 December***, *as the archive already held.* **The fourth time today that rule has stopped an error reaching the page.**

twins.heading: Twins, and the register says which came first
twins.lead: **The pedigree has given Franciscus Xaverius and Clotildis two daughters born on the same day since the tree was imported, and said nothing about it.** *Two rows with one date is ambiguous — it is as likely to be a copying error as a twin birth, and this archive has [found plenty of the first kind today](/corrections/).* **Folio 134 settles it in three words.**
paras:
> **«1868 Maji 31ma · [domus] 7 · MARIA HENRICA die 5 A[prilis] PRIUS NATA»**
> **«1868 Maji 31ma · [domus] 7 · CLOTILDIS ADELAIDIS die 5 Aprilis nata»**

*both of* «**Franciscus Defranceschi, possidens**» *and* «**Clotildis nata Ortis**»; *midwife* «Matthæa Stojsich». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069147, folio 134.)*

**⭐ *Prius nata* — born earlier.** *The priest wrote two entries for one birth and* ***marked the order of it***. **They are twins, born 5 April 1868, and Maria Henrica is the elder.** *This archive had both dates and no idea they belonged to one morning.*

**⚠ And the gap is long enough to be worth a line.** *Born* **5 April**, *baptised* **31 May** — ***fifty-six days***, *far longer than anything else this family shows. Maria Henrica's entry says she was* **«praesentata»**, *presented — the word used when a child has already been baptised privately, usually at birth and usually in danger, and is later brought to church for the ceremonies to be supplied.* **(The reading of that one word is offered and not leaned on.)** *Twins born to a household that could afford a midwife, and nearly two months before the font: the register is not explaining itself, but it is not hiding anything either.*

**⭐ AND EACH TWIN IS NAMED FOR HER GODPARENT.** *Maria* **HENRICA** *has* «**Henricus Defranceschi**» *for godfather. Clotildis* **ADELAIDIS** *has* «**Henricus Defranceschi**» *and* «**ADELAIDIS DEFRANCESCHI**», *the pair entered* **possidentes**.

**Those two are the brother and sister of the «et soror» entries.** *[Enrichus Jacobus, born 11 March 1830](/who/henricus-jacobus-defranceschi/) — whose baptism opened this day's work — and [Adelaidis](/who/adelaidis-defranceschi/), whom two of her brothers named a sister in 1847 and 1852 and who was* «unplaced» *in this archive until this afternoon.* ***Here they stand together at their brother's font, and his daughters are called after them.***

**⭐ Which is the strongest thing yet said about Adelaidis.** *[Worklist 175](/worklist/) holds the open question of whether she is the same child as* **Anastasia** *or* **Amelia**. *This does not answer it.* **But a woman who is chosen as a godmother in 1868, aged about forty-four, and has a niece named after her in the same entry, is a person with a life in this village** — *not a name that drifted into a pedigree. She was placed this afternoon on two godparent lines; she is confirmed this evening by a third and by a child.*

**And the house is still 7.** *Six children of this marriage are now documented there — [Anna Maria Francisca (1860)](/who/anna-maria-francisca-defranceschi/), [Victor Josephus (1862)](/who/victor-josephus-defranceschi/), [Amalia Lambertina (1863)](/gologorica-line/), [Beatrix Hermengildis (1865)](/person/hermenegildus-defranceschi-1865/) and these twins* — *in the house the 1826 census gives their grandfather.*

declaration.heading: A man who could not write acknowledges his son, and a Defranceschi witnesses it
declaration.lead: **Every Defranceschi in this book so far has appeared as a parent or a godparent.** *On the last day of 1870 one appears in a third role, and it is the one that says most about what the family was in this village.*
paras:
> **«Ego cum signo crucis signatus ANTONIUS RUP—OVIČ, agricola … declaro … esse verum me patrem hujus creaturæ ANTONII.»**
> *witnesses:* **«JOANNES DEFRANCESCHI»** *·* **«FRANCISCUS PALMAN»**

*Beside the baptism of* **30 December 1870**, *house* **26**, *the* Infans *column is given over to a declaration running the whole depth of the page. (doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069150, folio 140.)*

***«I, signed with the sign of the cross»*** *— the formula of a man who cannot write his own name. He is declaring, before the priest and two witnesses, that he is the true father of the child being baptised.* **A man who signs with a cross needs witnesses who can**, *and the parish found two.*

**⭐ One of them is a Defranceschi, and that is a role this archive has not seen the family in.** *Through ninety folios they are* **cives**, *then* **possidentes** *— words that assert standing. This is standing doing something:* ***being the literate neighbour whose name on a page makes another man's word binding.***

**Who he is, as an inference.** *The obvious candidate is* **[Joannes Baptista Defranceschi](/who/joannes-baptista-defranceschi/), born 19 June 1842** — *[whose own baptism was recovered today from the strip at the foot of a page](/corrections/)* — *the eldest son of Antonius and Francisca of house 5, twenty-eight years old and of exactly the age and class to be asked.* **(inf.)** *The register gives him no patronymic and no house, and this archive does not know another adult Joannes Defranceschi at Gologorica in 1870 — which is a reason to suspect, not a reason to assert.*

**And the second witness is a Palman**, *the family [whose surname cost this archive six days of public error](/corrections/). Here the two names stand side by side on one line, in one hand, three words apart.* ***It is the cleanest specimen of the two surnames together that the book has offered***, *and it says what the palaeographic test said in November 1843: they are not the same word and the parish never confused them.*

commissariato.heading: An Italian state office rules on the surname in 1920, and cites a birth certificate of 1626
commissariato.lead: **Folio 142 carries something no other page of this book carries: a typewriter.** *A slip of typed paper is pasted across the entries of 2 and 10 July 1871, hiding the baptisms underneath — and what it says reaches four hundred years back and out of Istria altogether.*
paras:
> **«Giusta lettera del Commissariato Gen. Civ. per la Venezia Giulia dd 10/12 1920 N. 1x-4411/563 la grafia originale del cognome di questo battezzato è “de Franceschi”, ciò che risulta dalla fede di nascita del suo proavo LEONARDO DE FRANCESCHI nato a LUINCIO dd. 23/6 1626.**
> **D’Ordine del Commissariato Gen. Civ. — Avv. Melone»**

*«By letter of the General Civil Commissariat for Venezia Giulia of 10 December 1920, no. 1x-4411/563, the original spelling of this baptised person’s surname is* **de Franceschi**, *as appears from the birth certificate of his forefather* **Leonardo de Franceschi, born at Luincio on 23 June 1626**.*» (doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069151, folio 142.)*

**What the office was.** *The* **Commissariato Generale Civile per la Venezia Giulia** *was the Italian civil administration of the territories annexed after 1918 — the body that ran Istria between the armistice and the full incorporation of 1922, and that spent much of its time regularising the names of people who had been Austrian subjects the year before.* ***This is a state act, signed by a lawyer, settling how a surname is to be written.***

**⭐ AND IT IS THE DEEPEST NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER BEEN HANDED.** *The [Carnia chain](/carnia/) begins with a* **Leonardo de Franceschi** *who is dead before 1785 and* ***known only from the way his son styles himself***. *Its deepest document is a parish certificate of 1808 reaching back to a* **Giovanni Battista** *dead by 1789. Here an Italian official says he had in front of him a* **fede di nascita** *— a birth certificate — for a* **Leonardo de Franceschi born at Luincis on 23 June 1626**.

**⚠ AND LUINCIS IS NOT A COINCIDENCE.** *[This archive has already quoted the Book of Baptisms of Luincis](/carnia/):* «Certifico io sottoscritto Parroco della **Pieve Matrice di Gorto a parte Luvincis**…» — *the certificate of 1808 that gave the family its deepest name.* ***The 1920 ruling cites the same parish’s register, a hundred and sixty-three years earlier.*** *The mother church of the Val Degano is where this family’s baptisms were kept, and an official in 1920 was reading its 1626 volume.*

**⚠ WHAT THIS IS NOT, and the list is long enough to matter.**

1. ***It is a 1920 ruling, not a 1626 record.*** *This archive has not seen the* fede di nascita. *An official says it existed and says what it contained.*
2. ***«Proavo» is being used loosely.*** *It means great-grandfather; 1626 to 1871 is seven or eight generations, not three. The word here means* **forefather**.
3. ***The office had a motive.*** *A body regularising surnames after annexation wants a spelling settled, and a settled spelling is not the same thing as a proved descent.* **Nothing here shows the official traced the line; it shows he accepted it.**
4. ***The slip hides the entry it annotates.*** *This archive cannot read the baptism underneath — which is a small, exact irony: the document that reaches furthest back is pasted over the one it is about.*

**⭐ AND THE FILM ANSWERS IT, because it photographed this opening twice.** *The very next frame,* **M01069152**, *is the same two pages with the slip* ***folded back***. *Underneath it:* «[domus] **7** · **VICTOR RICHARDUS die 15. Junii natus**» — *of* «**Defranceschi … possidens**» *and* «**[Clotilde] nata Ortis**»; *godparents* **Jodocus** *and* **Angelica Baxa**. *And in the margin of the entry, in the same hand as the slip:* **«vide … sub 30 protocoll.»** — ***see the document under protocol 30***, *a cross-reference from the register to the ruling.*

***So the 1920 act is about [Victor Richardus Defranceschi, born 15 June 1871, baptised 2 July](/who/victor-richardus-defranceschi/)*** — *a man of forty-nine in 1920, in exactly the position to need an Italian birth certificate.* **This was written up an hour ago as an inference. It is not one.**

**⭐ AND IT GIVES THE ARCHIVE TWO ADDRESSES INSTEAD OF A HOPE.**

* **The file itself** — *Commissariato Generale Civile per la Venezia Giulia,* **10 December 1920, N. 1x-4411/563**. *A numbered, dated act of a named office. Its records are state records.*
* **The register it cites** — *the baptisms of the* **Pieve di Gorto at Luincis for 1626**. *If an official read that book in 1920, the book existed in 1920.*

*[Worklist 179 carries both](/worklist/).* **For an archive whose Carnia origin has rested on Carlo De Franceschi’s own word and a chain of inference, a state document naming the place and the year is a different kind of thing — and it is still not the record itself.**

**⚠ And a note for whoever walks this film next.** *[The frame map](/gologorica-line/) records that these reels* «shoot some openings twice», *and [the coverage check](/searched/) treats a duplicate exposure as noise to be discounted.* ***Here the duplicate is the evidence.*** *One frame has the slip down and hides a baptism; the next has it lifted and shows both. **A second exposure of a page is not redundancy when something on that page can move.**

bookdone.heading: The baptism book is finished — 1784 to 1880, and its own index at the back
bookdone.lead: **One hundred and sixty-four folios, ninety-six years, and about a hundred and seventy frames.** *It was being sampled at every third frame when this week began. It is now walked end to end, both halves of every page — [after the crop that was cutting the feet off them was caught and the claim withdrawn](/corrections/) — and the book closes with something this archive did not know was there: ***its own alphabetical index***.
paras:
**⭐ THE INDEX NAMES THE TWO JOANNES BAPTISTA HOUSEHOLDS AND TELLS THEM APART.**

> **«Defranceschi Joan. Bapta defuncti Josephi · N.º 5»**
> *Joseph (p. 2) · Franciscus* (struck out) *· Catharina «quæ obiit» (p. 4) · Catharina Helena (p. 6) ·* **Maria Rosalia** *(p. 8) · Maria Antonia (p. 11)*

> **«Defranceschi Joanes Bapta DETTI LEONARDI · N.º 12»**
> *Franciscus Antonius (p. 3) · Joanes Bapta (p. 6)*

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069167.)*

***«Detti Leonardi» — called the Leonardi.*** *This archive has carried that byname [as the name of the casa-31 branch](/gologorica-line/), reasoned out of the family's habit of reusing the font-name Leonardus.* **Here it is in the register's own index, written by the priest who kept the book**, *and used for exactly what a byname is for: telling two men called Joannes Baptista Defranceschi apart.*

**⭐ And it bridges the two numbering systems.** *The archive's* **casa 31** *is the* «detti Leonardi» *household; the index calls that household* **N.º 12**. *[Worklist 171 has been asking since this morning what the book's second series of house numbers is](/worklist/) — and this is the first place where a household appears under a number from each.* ***31 and 12 are the same door.*** *(One pair is not a key, and the item stays open; but it is the first pair that comes with a name attached rather than a strike-through.)*

**⭐ CARLO DE FRANCESCHI STANDS AT THE FONT.**

> **«1874 Octob. 11 · [domus] 11 · FRANCISCUS CAROLUS NATALIS die 6. Octob. natus · Franciscus Defranceschi, possidens · Clotildis nata Ortis · CARLO DEFRANCESCHI, Natale Stipanich · cives»** — *with* **«† Tergeste 17-2-1942»** *in the margin. (doc — M01069156, folio 150.)*

*[Carlo De Franceschi](/carlo/) — born 17 October 1809, died 8 January 1893, the historian this entire archive leans on — standing godfather to his brother's son* **six days before his own sixty-fifth birthday**. ***And the child carries both godparents' names: Carolus for Carlo, Natalis for Natale Stipanich.*** *The archive has Carlo's writings, his letter, his book and his grave. This is the first time it has him in the register of his own village doing an ordinary family thing.*

**⭐ THREE DEFRANCESCHI HOUSEHOLDS THE ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE.**

| father | wife | children found |
|---|---|---|
| **Aloysius Defranceschi, *mercator*** | **Joanna née Udovicic** | **Elvira Gisella** b. 15 Apr 1873 · **Ersilia** b. 8 Dec 1878 |
| **[Leonardus Defranceschi](/who/leonardus-defranceschi/), *textor*** (house 6) | **Maria née Flegar** | **Carola** b. 22 Mar 1875 · **Joannes Aloysius** b. 4 Nov 1876 · **Theresia** b. 17 Mar 1879 |
| *Fortunatus Sestan, agricola* (house 9) | **Rosa née DEFRANCESCHI** | **Maria Anna** b. 19 Oct 1877 |

**⚠ AND THE FIRST OF THEM IS A PROBLEM.** *This archive carries* **[Aloysius Defranceschi, born 8 May 1832 at Volosca, died 25 November 1870](/who/aloysius-defranceschi/)** — *Carlo's brother, [the one whose birthplace was corrected from «Polonia» to «Volosca»](/gologorica-line/).* ***A man who died in 1870 cannot father a daughter in April 1873.*** *So either this is a second Aloysius Defranceschi at Gologorica, or the 1870 death belongs to somebody else.* **Nothing is changed on his record**; *it is [the fourth unresolved death-year collision in this family](/gologorica-line/), and it goes on the same pile — which is now the strongest argument on this site for opening the burial register.*

**⭐ And Rosa closes a circle this archive opened this morning.** *At eight o'clock today a child the family tree called* «Joanna, born 9 June 1848» *was shown by her own baptism to be* **[Rosa, born 7 June 1848](/person/joanna-defranceschi-1848/)**, *dead 10 December 1899.* *At the far end of the book she is married to* **Fortunatus Sestan** — *the second son of* **[Sancta Alexandra Defranceschi](/who/sancta-alexandra-defranceschi-sestan/)**, *whose empty note was filled the same morning.* ***Two Defranceschi daughters married into the Sestan house of Gologorica in the 1840s; in the next generation a Defranceschi daughter marries their son.*** **(inf** *that this Rosa is that Rosa — the archive knows no other Rosa Defranceschi of the age at Gologorica, which is a reason to suspect and not to assert.)*

**⭐ And Sancta Alexandra is the parish midwife.** *Her name is in the* Obstetrix *column in* **1873** *and again in* **1876** — *«Sancta Sestan», delivering the village's children at fifty-four and fifty-seven, including [Lambertina Lina Defranceschi](/who/lambertina-lina-defranceschi/)'s.* **A woman this archive held at breakfast with an empty note, no husband and no children: ten children of her own, a trade, and a place in every household in the village.**

**And the 1920 ruling is on the page twice.** *[The typewritten slip over Victor Richardus's entry](/gologorica-line/) is not the only copy:* ***the same text is written out by hand at the foot of folio 150***, *over the entry of Franciscus Carolus Natalis. The signature is clearer there —* **«Avv. Mellone»**. *So the Commissariato's act was applied to the baptisms of at least two brothers, which is what regularising a family's papers looks like.*

**What is left of the reel.** *The baptism book is done. On the same two reels, unread or barely touched:* **the Gologorica deaths 1784–1880 (91 frames, ~2%)**, **Cerovlje's status animarum (139 frames, never opened)**, *and the* **1862, 1894 and 1921** *household censuses.* ***The death book is next, and [the case for it is already written](/gologorica-line/).***

deathbook1.heading: The death book opens, and answers in two pages what the archive had argued for a fortnight
deathbook1.lead: **The register of the dead of Gologorica, 1784 to 1880 — ninety-one frames, barely two per cent of it read, and [the case for opening it was written yesterday](/gologorica-line/) on the strength of four unresolved death years.** *It has an alphabetical index at the back, as the baptism book does. The index names the pages. The first two pages the index pointed at settled the two oldest questions on this page.*
paras:
> **«1821. Die 30ma Januarii hora ½ 4ta a meridie · [domus] 104 · CLEMENTINA FILIA D.ni JOSEPHI DEFRANCESCHI · dierum 2 et horarum 11½ · Imperfecta Structura»**
> *Sepulta fuit die 1ma Februarii 1821. — Ant. Ferdinandus Mocovich, parochus.*

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069259, page 62.)*

**⭐ THE TWO CLEMENTINAS ARE NO LONGER A QUESTION.** *[Her baptism](/gologorica-line/), in the other book, has her* **born 28 January 1821 at four in the morning, at house 104**. *This entry has her dead on* **30 January at half past three in the afternoon**, *at house 104, aged* **two days and eleven and a half hours**. ***From four in the morning on the 28th to half past three on the afternoon of the 30th is two days and eleven and a half hours. The arithmetic closes exactly.***

**So the elder Clementina died at two days old, of *imperfecta structura* — imperfect formation — and her parents gave the name again to [the daughter born 3 October 1822](/person/clementina-maria-defranceschi-1822/).** *This archive inferred that on 1 October, from nothing but the twenty-month gap and what families do.* **The inference was right, and it is now a document.** *[And yesterday's caution was right too](/gologorica-line/): her baptism carries no marginal cross, and a blank margin in that book means nothing at all.*

**⚠ And it moves a death year that was sitting on the wrong woman.** *This roster gave the 1821 Clementina a death of* **1870**. *She died in 1821.* ***So the 1870 cannot be hers***, *and [the thirty-year dispute over the 1822 Clementina](/corrections/) — archive 1840 against tree 1870 — loses one of its two explanations: it can no longer be settled by saying the 1870 belongs to her sister.* **Both rows are corrected and the remaining dispute is stated, not resolved.**

**⭐ And it identifies the godmother of 1840.** *[A Clementina Defranceschi stood godmother at Gologorica on 20 February 1840](/gologorica-line/), entered* **civis**, *and this archive wrote that she might be either of the two.* ***She cannot be the elder. There is only one Clementina left.***

> **«1817. Die 19 Xbris hora 10ma noctis · [domus] 17 · MAXIMILIANUS JOSEPH DEFRANCESCHI, D.ni Josephi filius · annorum 4 · Vermes et Phthisis cum febri maligna»**
> *Sepultus fuit die 20 … Solis occasum* **ob signa putrefactionis**. *(doc — M01069257, page 58.)*

**⭐ A SON THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE, AND A SECOND NAME REUSED.** *Four years old in December 1817, so* ***born about 1813*** — *between [Maria Aloysia](/person/maria-defranceschi-1811/) (August 1811) and [Franciscus Xaverius](/gologorica-line/) (February 1816), in a gap the pedigree had empty.* **The Maximilianus Antonius this archive knows was born 8 January 1828** — *[his baptism was found on Sunday](/gologorica-line/)* — ***eleven years after this child was buried.***

**So Josephus and Lambertina reused two names, not one.** *Clementina in 1822 for the daughter of 1821; Maximilianus in 1828 for the son of about 1813.* ***That is no longer an inference about what families did. It is the documented habit of this family***, *and it is a warning to anyone matching a Gologorica Defranceschi by given name alone.*

**⚠ And the burial tells you what December 1817 was like.** *He was buried* **the next day at sunset, «ob signa putrefactionis»** — *because of the signs of putrefaction. The page around him is dense with children: worms, consumption, malignant fever, a four-year-old, a two-year-old, an infant of five months.* **The register of a village in a bad winter.**

**What the index gives, which is a map of the rest.** *Under* «Defranceschi **Joseph · N.º 17**» *the book lists fourteen deaths with their pages — among them* **«R.dus Joan: Mathias, ex Parochus» (p. 15)**, *a Defranceschi who had been parish priest;* **«D.na Helena, vidua q. Josephi» (p. 25)**; **«D.nus Joan: Bapta q. Josephi» (p. 39)**; *and* **«Amalia, filia Josephi» (p. 67)**. *Two further households follow —* «Joanes Bapta **detti Leonardi** · N.º 12» *and* «**Leonardus** · N.º 10». ***The index was read in this archive before. Its pages had never been opened.***

deathbook2.heading: A Defranceschi who had been parish priest of Gračišće
deathbook2.lead: **The death book's index lists fourteen Defranceschi under house 17, and the third of them is a title rather than a name:** «R.dus Joan: Mathias, **ex Parochus**». *This archive held that man as a bare row with the single word* **«Don»** *against it, no dates, no place beyond Gologorica. Page 15 gives him everything.*
paras:
> **«Idem · [domus] 63 · 29 Martij [1798] · admodum R[everen]d[u]s D[omi]n[u]s MATH. DE FRANCESCHI, ex Parocho GALLEGNA[nensi] · annorum 62 · Paralisia»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069235, page 15 of the death register.)*

**⭐ *Ex Parocho Gallignanensi* — formerly parish priest of GALLIGNANA, which is GRAČIŠĆE.** *Not a neighbouring parish picked at random:* ***[Gračišće is where the Eleven are](/the-eleven/), and it is this line's own second home*** — *the parish [Francisca](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1819/) and [Joanna](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/) came out of, the parish whose registers sit on the one reel the family does not hold.* **A man of this surname held that cure, and died at Gologorica on 29 March 1798, aged sixty-two, of a stroke.** *Born about 1736.*

**What the archive had instead.** *A roster row —* `joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica` — *carrying his name, the place «Gologorica», the line «carnia», and for a note the word* **«Don»**. *That is all. He was a title somebody had written down and nobody had looked for.*

**⚠ And it is a lead, not a conclusion, about where he fits.** *The entry gives his age and his office and* ***not his father***. *The index files him under* «Defranceschi **Joseph · N.º 17**», *which is the household this archive follows — but an index is a clerk's filing decision, not a statement of descent.* **No parent is attached to him on the strength of it.** *What is now worth doing is asking the Gračišće registers who their priest was in the 1760s–1790s, which [is on the reel that is already the first errand](/errands/).*

> **«Idem · [domus] 36 · 26 augusti [1804] · D.na HELLENA, vid[ua] q. JOSEPHI DEFRANCESCHI ex loco · annorum 84 · Maligna»**

*(doc — M01069240, page 25.)*

**⭐ Domina Helena, widow of the late Josephus Defranceschi, dead of a malignant fever at eighty-four.** *Eighty-four in August 1804 puts her birth about* **1720**. *This archive carries her as* **1725–1809**. ***The register disagrees with it at both ends*** — *four years on the birth and five on the death.*

**⚠ That is the fifth collision in this family, and the first the death book has produced rather than closed.** *[The other four](/worklist/) are Clementina, Josephus Lambertus, Antonius and Aloysius. **This one is different in kind**: it is not a tree against an archive guess, it is a* ***contemporary parish entry against a date this archive has published***, *and the parish entry is the better-placed of the two.* **Nothing is changed on her row yet** — *the book is four frames in, and the sensible thing is to finish it before moving dates one at a time.*

**And the dean signed both books on the same day.** *Ruled across page 25, above Helena:* «**Revisus in Visitatione Decanali die 17ma Julii 1804** — M. Franciscus Franovich, Canonicus, Cæsareus Regius Parochus et Decanus». ***The same inspection, the same date and the same dean that [this archive found in the baptism book](/worklist/)*** — *so a visitation signed every register in the parish on one visit, and [worklist 169](/worklist/) can expect its protocols to cover all three books rather than one.*

french1812.heading: The French took the registers, and the priest wrote down what that cost him
french1812.lead: **Between two deaths of 1812, ruled across the column in the parish priest's own hand, is the only sentence in these books about who owned them.**
paras:
> **«N.B. Hic Liber cum aliis ex justa ordinationem regiminis GALLICI consignatus fuit MUNICIPALITATI PISINENSI die 20ma Julii 1812, et die 5ta Januarii 1814 fuere restituti ab Administratione Dominali; quamobrem Mortuorum eorum Nomina, qui per hoc intervallum obierunt, fideliter ex more solito hic retuli: ego idem Parochus Mocovich qui supra.»**

*«This book with the others, by the just ordinance of the* **French** *government, was consigned to the* **Municipality of Pazin** *on* **20 July 1812**, *and on* **5 January 1814** *they were restored by the Seigneurial Administration; wherefore the names of those who died during this interval I have faithfully entered here in the usual way: I, the same parish priest Mocovich as above.»* *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069247, page 38 of the death register.)*

**⭐ For eighteen months this parish did not have its own registers.** *Istria was inside Napoleon's* **Illyrian Provinces**, *and the French did what the French did everywhere: they took registration off the church and gave it to the commune.* ***The books went to Pazin on 20 July 1812 and came back on 5 January 1814.***

**⚠ WHICH MAKES EVERY DATE IN THIS BOOK BETWEEN THOSE TWO DAYS A RETROSPECTIVE ONE.** *The priest says so himself:* «quamobrem … fideliter ex more solito **hic retuli**» — ***wherefore I have entered them here afterwards.*** *He is not hiding it; he is flagging it, which is more than most registers do.* **But an entry written up from memory or from a note eighteen months later is not an entry made on the day**, *and any Gologorica date this archive holds from* **July 1812 to January 1814** *should be read with that in front of it.*

**⭐ AND IT NAMES A RECORD SERIES THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER LOOKED FOR.** *If the commune held registration for eighteen months,* ***the commune registered***. *There should be* **French civil registers of the Municipality of Pazin, 1812–1814** — *births, marriages and deaths for every parish in its district, Gologorica among them.* **This archive has never asked for them**, *and they are the only contemporary record of that window. [Worklist 180](/worklist/) carries it.*

**And beneath it, a nil — recorded by a parish priest in 1812.**

> **«N.B. A die 10ma Julii usque ad 19am Augusti exclusive nemo obiit in hac Parochia.»**

*«From 10 July to 19 August exclusive, nobody died in this parish.»* ***He wrote down an absence, with its exact bounds, so that nobody reading after him would mistake a silent page for a lost one.*** *[It is the rule this archive works to](/method/), set down in the same book two hundred and fourteen years earlier.*

> **«Die 22 Xbris 1826 hora 3tia postm. · [domus] 17 · AMALIA DE FRANCESCHI, filia Josephi · 8 Men[ses] · febres gastricæ, mali[gnæ]»** — *buried the 24th at ten in the morning. (doc — M01069262, page 67.)*

**⭐ Amalia had no dates at all.** *The pedigree carried her as a child of* **Josephus and Lambertina** *with neither birth nor death — a name in a list.* *She died on* **22 December 1826 aged eight months**, *of gastric and malignant fever, at house 17, and was buried two days later.* ***Born about April 1826.***

**⭐ And it unpicks one strand of a knot.** *[Worklist 175](/worklist/) holds four names round one household —* **Anastasia**, **Maria Adelgidis**, **Adelaidis** *and* **Amelia** — *and asks how many children they are.* ***Amalia died in infancy, so she cannot be the Adelaidis who stands godmother in 1847, in 1852 and at the twins' font in 1868.*** **One of the four is now accounted for, and the question narrows to whether Adelaidis and Anastasia are one girl.**

parochus.heading: A Defranceschi buried this parish — the surname is in the officiant column
parochus.lead: **The leftmost column of a death register is *Sepeliens*: who performed the burial.** *For most of this book it reads* «Mocovich», «Bobich», «Brussich», «Zwölber» — *the priests [the parish-house list names](/gologorica-line/). At the head of the year* **1787** *it reads something else.*
paras:
> **«[Defran]CESCHI, P[aro]CHUS LOCI»**

*Defranceschi, parish priest of this place — and the entries beneath run* «Idem», *the same man, down the page. (doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069230, page 5 of the death register.)*

**⭐ A man of this surname was burying the people of Gologorica in 1787 and 1788**, *and signing for it in the column that says who did. Not a visiting priest borrowed for a day —* ***Parochus Loci***, *the parish priest of the place.*

**And [the entry on page 15 is almost certainly the same man](/gologorica-line/).** *«Admodum R.dus D.nus* **MATH. DE FRANCESCHI, ex Parocho GALLEGNA[nensi]**», *dead 29 March 1798 aged sixty-two.* ***So a priest of this name held Gologorica in the 1780s and had held, or went on to hold, Gallignana — which is [Gračišće](/the-eleven/), this line's own second home.***

**⚠ One man or two is not settled by these two pages, and the archive says so.** *The 1798 entry styles him by* **Gallignana** *and not by Gologorica, which is what you would expect of a man who had retired from the local cure years before —* «ex Parochus», *as [the book's own index calls him](/gologorica-line/).* ***The index lists only one Defranceschi priest***, *which favours one man with two cures.* **It does not prove it.** *The Gračišće registers would, and they are [on the reel that is already the first errand](/errands/).*

**What this does to a surname.** *This archive has spent the week watching the Defranceschi of Gologorica be entered* **civis** *and then* **possidens** — *words that assert standing.* ***A parish priest of the village, of the same name, in the 1780s, is what that standing looked like a generation earlier***, *and it is the reason a Defranceschi child could have [a canon and dean for a godfather](/gologorica-line/) in 1828.*

> **«Admodum R.dus D.nus Martinus Sestan, PAROCHUS NOVACENSIS, de licentia mea parochi presentis · [domus] 17 · Die 23. Januarii 1813 · D.nus JOANNES BAPTA DEFRANCESCHI, VIDUUS, defuncti Josephi filius · annorum 60 · Phthisis»**

*(doc — M01069248, page 39.)*

**⭐ The head of house 17 and of the titled branch, dead at sixty of consumption.** *This archive holds him as* **born about October 1752, died 23 January 1813**, *with the note* «Dominus» *and nothing else.* ***The register agrees with the date to the day*** — *verification, not discovery — and adds the rest: he died a* **widower**, *son of the late Josephus, at* **house 17**, *of* **phthisis**, *aged sixty years and three days over the months.*

**And he was buried by the parish priest of Novaki.** «Martinus Sestan, **Parochus Novacensis**, *de licentia mea parochi presentis*» — *by licence of me, the present parish priest.* *[Novaki is where Clotilda Ortis came from](/gologorica-line/), two generations later. The parishes of this corner lent each other priests constantly, and [the baptism book showed the same of Krbune](/worklist/).*

**⚠ And a trap recorded so the next reader does not fall into it.** *Three rows below him stands* **«Josephus DE-PRATO, cœlebs, defuncti Joannis Baptæ filius»**, *a student of twenty-five dead of consumption in the same March.* ***At page scale the broken surname reads as a Defranceschi***, *and a man of that age dying two months after Joannes Baptista, styled son of the late Joannes Baptista, is exactly what one would want him to be.* **He is a Deprato.** *The line break did it. [It is the fourth time this week a reading has had to be cut past its own cell](/corrections/).*

house36.heading: House 36, in eighteen months
house36.lead: **[The man who died a widower in 1813](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1752/) became one on a page this archive had never opened.** *Three Defranceschi deaths stand within eighteen months at house 36, and between them they turn a line in a pedigree into a sequence.*
paras:
| when | who | age | cause | buried by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **16 July 1791** | **Maria Antonia Defranceschi** | ***six months*** | *vermes* | «Defranceschi, Parochus» |
| **26 April 1792** | **Sancta Defranceschi, *cœlebs*** | **58** | *febris putrida* | **Joh. Marinich, *Canon of Gallignana*** |
| **21 May 1792** | **Catharina Defranceschi** | **26** | *apoplexia* | **Petrus Anicich, *priest of Novaki*** |

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069233, pages 11–12 of the death register.)*

**⭐ CATHARINA IS THE JABLICH, AND SHE HAD NO DATES AT ALL.** *[This archive knows her](/married-in/) from a single line of the baptism book — «**Joh: Bapt. Defranceschi m.p. · Cath. ejus uxor nata JABLICH ex BUCCARI**», both* **Cives Gollogoricenses**, *standing as godparents on 3 October 1786 — and from nothing else.* ***She died on 21 May 1792, aged twenty-six, of apoplexy.*** *Born about 1766, she was twenty when she stood at that font and twenty-six when she was carried out of house 36.*

**⭐ And ten months before her, their daughter.** *«**MARIA ANTONIA DEFRANCESCHI** · mens[ium]* **6** *· Vermes», 16 July 1791.* *This archive carried a* **Maria Antonia born 1791** *off the family tree with no death; the register gives the death and confirms the birth —* ***she was six months old.***

**So the shape of it is this.** *Joannes Baptista Defranceschi buried a daughter of six months in* **July 1791**, *and his wife of twenty-six in* **May 1792**. ***He did not remarry. He died a widower twenty-one years later, in January 1813, at sixty.*** *The pedigree had the two dates at either end and nothing in between; the death book is what joins them.*

**⭐ And a woman the archive did not have at all.** *«**SANCTA DEFRANCESCHI, CŒLEBS** · annorum* **58**», *26 April 1792 — unmarried, born about* **1734**, *dead four weeks before Catharina in the same house.* **A spinster aunt of the household, and no roster row anywhere for her.**

**⚠ GRAČIŠĆE KEEPS TURNING UP AT THIS FAMILY'S GRAVESIDE.** *Sancta was buried by* **«Joh. Marinich, Canonicus GALLIGNANENSIS»** — *a canon of Gračišće.* *With [the Defranceschi priest styled* «ex Parocho Gallignanensi» *](/gologorica-line/), that is the second churchman of that parish standing over this family inside a decade.* ***It is a pattern and not yet a reason***, *and what would turn it into one is the Gračišće register on [the reel that is the first errand](/errands/).*

**And one small tie that costs nothing to notice.** *Catharina was buried by* **«Petrus Anicich, P[res]b[yte]r Novacensis»** — *the priest of Novaki.* ***[Worklist 169](/worklist/) already names a «Petrus Anicich» as the DEAN who inspected this parish in 1808.*** *Sixteen years apart, the same man: a village priest in 1792, a rural dean by 1808. The deanery was staffed from the parishes it inspected.*

deprato.heading: ⚠ The family that is not this one — DEPRATO of house 6
