deprato.lead: **Yesterday a student of twenty-five, dead of consumption in March 1813 and styled «son of the late Joannes Baptista», was very nearly written into this archive as a Defranceschi.** *He was a* **Deprato**, *and the line break did it.* ***The death book's index shows that it was not a near miss. It was a trap with a shape.***
paras:
| **DEFRANCESCHI · Joseph, N.º 17** | | **DEPRATO · Leonardus, N.º 6** | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catharina, **uxor Joan: Baptæ** | p. 12 | Cattarina, **uxor Joan: Baptæ** | p. 24 |
| **R.dus Joan: Mathias, *ex Parochus*** | p. 15 | **R.dus Joseph Deprato, *Ex Parochus*** | p. 20 |
| **D.nus Joan: Bapta** q. Josephi | p. **39** | **Joannes Bapta, *viduus*** | p. 32 |
| Helena, ***vidua*** q. Josephi | p. 25 | Catharina, ***vidua*** q. Leonardi | p. 50 |
| — | | **Josephus, *filius q. Joan: Baptæ*** | p. **39** |

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069301, the death book's own index.)*

**⭐ Two families in one village, and the same five people.** *Each has a* **Joannes Baptista**; *each has a* **Catharina who is the wife of a Joannes Baptista**; *each has a* **Reverend former parish priest**; *each has a* **widow**; *and the Deprato have a* **Josephus, son of the late Joannes Baptista**, *where the Defranceschi have a* **Dominus Joannes Baptista, son of the late Josephus**.

**⚠ AND BOTH OF THOSE LAST TWO ARE ON PAGE 39.** *That is the page [this archive read yesterday](/gologorica-line/).* ***The Defranceschi head of house dies there on 23 January 1813, and three rows below him the Deprato student dies on 12 March*** — *and the index put them on the same page because the clerk was filing two families whose men had the same names.*

**⚠ AND BOTH SURNAMES BEGIN «De—» AND BREAK ACROSS LINES.** *In a narrow column a scribe writes* «Defran-ceschi» *and* «De-prato», *and at page scale the second reads as the first.* ***That is not a coincidence of handwriting. It is a coincidence of handwriting on top of a coincidence of names, in one parish, in one book.***

**What this archive is doing about it.** *Nothing is merged, nothing is split, and no Deprato is entering the roster — they are not this surname and [this is a one-name study](/method/).* **What is published is the warning**, *because the next person to walk these books will meet it:*

> ***At Gologorica, a «De—» surname with a Joannes Baptista, a Catharina his wife, a Josephus his son and a Reverend ex-parish-priest may be a Defranceschi or a Deprato. Read the second syllable, past the line break, before you write the name down.***

**And two more Defranceschi deaths from the earliest pages, where the priest of the parish was one of them.**

> **«Idem · [domus] 36 · 12 Martij 1786 · CATHAR[INA] DEFRANCESCHI ex loco · dier[um] 11 · Debilitas»**
> **«Idem · [domus] 31 · 4 8bris 1786 · MARIANA DEFRANCESCHI · annorum 10 · Dissenteria»**

*(doc — M01069229, page 3.)*

***Catharina, eleven days old*** — *the first child of [Joannes Baptista and Catharina née Jablich](/who/catharina-defranceschi-jablich/), born about 1 March 1786 and dead on the 12th, five years before [the six-month-old Maria Antonia](/who/maria-antonia-defranceschi/) and six before her mother.* **That household buried three in six years.**

***Mariana, aged ten, of dysentery*** — *and she is at* **house 31**, *not 36.* **So she belongs to the other branch, the «detti Leonardi»** — *and the index files her under* «Defranceschi Joanes Bapta **detti Leonardi · N.º 12**». ***Which is the second independent confirmation that house 31 and index number 12 are the same door***, *after [the baptism book's index said the same thing yesterday](/gologorica-line/). [Worklist 171](/worklist/) now has two anchored pairs instead of one.*

**And the officiant column pushes the Defranceschi priest back a year.** *«Defrances[chi] P[res]b[yte]r Loci» heads the year* **1786**, *not 1787 as this archive wrote yesterday.* *A small correction to a sentence of its own, made before anyone else had to make it.*

threedes.heading: Three «De—» surnames on one page, and the rule earns its keep the same day
threedes.lead: **This archive published a rule a few hours ago:** *at Gologorica a* «De—» *surname with a Joannes Baptista and a Reverend ex-parish-priest may be a Defranceschi or a* **Deprato**, ***so read the second syllable past the line break before writing the name down***. *The next page it opened contained a case. It also contained a third family.*
paras:
> **«Defrances[chi] · [domus] 84 · 10 Augusti 1788 · ANTONIO DE-FRANICH · annorum 70 · febris putrida»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069231, page 7 of the death register.)*

**⭐ «DE-FRANICH», not Defranceschi.** *At page scale the entry reads as one of ours — an Antonio of seventy, in the family's own parish, with the surname broken after* «De». ***Cut past the line break and the second syllable is* «franich» *— the same opening and a different family.*** **No row is minted and nothing enters the roster.**

**⚠ So there are at least THREE «De—» families in this one village**, *and the officiant column of this very page shows two of them working side by side:*

| | |
|---|---|
| «**DEFRANCES[CHI]**, *P[res]b[yte]r Loci*» | *the parish priest of this place* |
| «**D. JOSEPH: DEPRATO**, *ex Paroch[us]*» | *a former parish priest* |
| «**ANTONIO DE-FRANICH**» | *the man being buried* |

***Two priests of two different families alternate down the column, and a third family is in the entries beneath them.*** *[Worklist 183](/worklist/) is updated from two surnames to three.*

**And the rule was applied backwards as well as forwards.** *Two entries this archive published yesterday had been read at the first syllable only.* ***Both were re-cropped past the line break and both hold:***

> «Maria Anton: **Defranceschi**» *(page 11) — written out in full on one line.*
> «D.na Hellena, Vid. q. Joseph: **Defran-ceschi** ex Loco» *(page 25) — the second line reads* «ceschi».

**Neither needed a correction. The point of checking was that this archive could not have known that without looking**, *and it had already been wrong once.*

**⚠ And the honest consequence.** *Every Defranceschi this archive has read off these two reels where the surname was broken across a line is now a thing to re-check, not a thing to trust.* ***That is not a retraction — none of the published readings has failed — it is a backlog***, *and [worklist 183](/worklist/) carries it with the list of where to start.*

smallpox1789.heading: Smallpox, September 1789 — a child from each Defranceschi house, nine days apart
smallpox1789.lead: **The cause column of page 8 says *Pustulla* almost all the way down.** *Seven of the nine entries in the lower half of that page are smallpox, and two of them are this family's.*
paras:
> **«Idem · [domus] 31 · 10 7bris 1789 · JOH. DEFRAN-CESCHI, fil. Ther[esiæ] · annorum 7 · Pustulla»**
> **«Idem · [domus] 36 · 19 7bris 1789 · JOSEPH. DEFRAN-CESCHI ex Loco · annorum 5 · Pustulla»**

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069231, page 8 of the death register.)*

**⭐ Both Defranceschi households buried a child inside nine days.** *A boy of seven from* **house 31** — *the* «detti Leonardi» *branch — and a boy of five from* **house 36**, *[the house that would bury three more in the six years after](/gologorica-line/).* ***Neither child is anywhere in this archive.*** *They were born about 1782 and 1784 and nothing recorded them but their deaths.*

**⭐ And the elder is named for his mother.** «Joh: Defranceschi, **fil. Theriæ**» — *son of Theresia.* *The archive knows exactly one Theresia of house 31:* **[Theresia née Grach](/worklist/)**, *the wife whose family gave this archive [the Krbune question](/worklist/) — the Grach of «Cherbune», with an archpriest among them.* **So this is her son.**

**⚠ Why a mother and not a father, this archive does not know.** *Every other child on the page is* «ex Loco» *or* «filius [N.]». *A boy identified by his mother may mean a father dead, a father absent, or nothing at all but the clerk's hand.* ***It is recorded because it is unusual and not because it is understood.***

**What the page is.** *An epidemic, told in a column. Maria Cosara of twenty-seven and Maria Cosara of six days; Vitus Selesco of thirty days; Joh. Bapt. Gasparich of three months; Mathæus Delgor Zaicich of sixteen days; Antonius Pascoli of one; Catharina Pascoli, wife of Josephus, of twenty-two. And two Defranceschi boys.* **This archive has walked a hundred and sixty folios of baptisms and has almost nothing on how this village died. One page of the other book gives more than all of them.**

**And it is the argument for this book restated.** *[The case for opening the death register](/gologorica-line/) was four disputed dates. **It has now produced, in a day: two settled questions, a fifth collision, three people with no row anywhere, a parish priest of the family, two more surnames to beware of, an eighteen-month gap under the French, and an epidemic.*** *None of that was on the list.*

antonius1802.heading: A man the archive had only from the family tree — and the index that calls him Leonardo's father
antonius1802.lead: **Antonius Defranceschi, born 1742, died 1802.** *That is the whole of what this archive knew about him, and every word of it came off [the family tree](/people/). No register, no ark, no film, no note — a row with two years in it and nothing holding them up.* **Page 21 of the Gologorica death book holds them up, to the day.**
paras:
> *Gologorica deaths, image M01069238, page 21, the third entry under the year* **1802**:
> «Idem · **29.** · **17 7mbris** · t. · **Antonius De=franceschi ex Loco** · t. — t. — · **ann[orum] 60.** · **Hectica**»

**House 29. Dead 17 September 1802. Male, catholic, aged sixty. Of hectica** — *the wasting consumption, which is what this book calls tuberculosis.* ***Sixty years in September 1802 puts his birth about 1742 — which is the year the tree gives.*** *(doc.)*

**⚠ The birth year is still the tree's, and it is worth being exact about why.** *An age at death implies a year; it does not state one. The register and the tree agree, and agreement from two directions is worth a great deal — but* **1742** *remains an implied year, not a recorded one, and [this archive does not promote an implied year to a declared one](/method/). What changed today is the* **death**, *which is now a document rather than a tree entry.*

**⭐ And the book's own index does something the entry does not: it gives him a household and a son.**

*Among the «D» blocks on image M01069301, between* «Defranceschi Joseph N.º 17» *and* «Deprato Leonardus N.º 6», *stands a third heading —* **«Defranceschi Leonardus N.º 10»** — *and under it exactly one name:*

> **«Antonius Leonardi pater · 21.»**

***Antonius, Leonardo's father. Page 21.*** *The page is the one above. The priest indexing this book filed him not under his own name but under his son's house.*

**So the index names three Defranceschi households and one that only looks like a fourth:** «**Joseph** N.º 17», «**Joanes Bapta detti Lonardi** N.º 12» *— the byname [that bridged casa 31 to N.12 in the baptism book's index](/gologorica-line/) —* «**Leonardus** N.º 10», *and then* «**Deprato** Leonardus N.º 6», *[which is not this family at all](/gologorica-line/). **Four «De—» headings on one index page, and only three of them are ours.***

**⚠ AND HERE IS A TRAP WORTH SETTING A SIGN IN FRONT OF, because the archive already holds its mirror image.** *This man is* **«Antonius, Leonardi PATER»** — *Antonius the* **father** *of Leonardo. The archive also holds* **«[Antonio q. Leonardo de Franceschi da Gollogorizza](/person/antonio-de-franceschi-q-leonardo-of-gologorica-m-1785-svetvincenat/)»**, *who married at Svetvinčenat on 14 March 1785 — Antonio the* **son** *of the late Leonardo.* ***Two Antonios, each defined by a Leonardo, in opposite directions.*** *Set side by side the phrases are nearly the same words; they describe men a generation apart. The 1785 bridegroom's father was already dead; this man was alive until 1802 and was somebody's father, not somebody's son.* **They are not the same person, and nothing yet joins them.**

*What would join them — or separate them for good — is the page the index points at for Leonardus N.º 10's own death, and the marriage book that would name Antonius's wife. Neither has been opened.* **[Logged, not claimed.](/worklist/)**

deathwalk1.heading: Walking the death book from the cover — bells, two epidemics, and a column that says «hunger»
deathwalk1.lead: *The death book had been opened at pages its own index pointed to. This is the first stretch* **walked** *— cover to page 22, 1784 to 1803, every entry of every page read rather than scanned for one surname.* **No Defranceschi died in any of these pages beyond the ones already published** *— and that nil is worth as much as a hit, because it is now a* ***named*** *nil. What the walk did turn up is the parish around them.*
paras:
**⭐ FIRST, A RECORD TYPE NOBODY HAD CATALOGUED — and it is not in Latin.**

*Inside the front cover, on the flyleaf before the register proper, are five entries in* **Italian**, *1801 to 1805, each to the same formula:*

> «Gollogoriza 30 Agosto 1801 **è passata da questa alla miglior vita Ellena Moglie di Gio: Udonich q. Francesco**, fù dato un Ducato o sian **L. 6 alla Chiesa per suono di tutte tre Campane**.»

***A ducat — six lire — to the church, for the ringing of all three bells.*** *Five families paid it: Udovicich, Marion, Sestan, Zubran, Peer.* **No Defranceschi among them**, *which is itself a fact about what this family did or did not buy.*

**⚠ And it is a payment ledger, not a second death register — the dates prove it.** *Three of the five can be matched to the Latin register by name:* **Ellena Udovicich** *appears there under* **30 August 1801**, *the same day;* **Catharina Marion vidua q.m Antonij** *under 3 March where the flyleaf says 2 March;* **Catharina uxor Joh: Sestan alij Pedre** *under* **13 June** *where the flyleaf says* **29 June** *— sixteen days apart.* ***So the two books record the same deaths and count different events.*** *Which event the Italian date marks — the burial, the ringing, or the paying — this archive does not yet know, and says so.*

**⭐ THE DEPRATO PRIEST NOW HAS DATES, which matters because his surname is the one that keeps being mistaken for ours.**

> *p. 20, 17 October 1801, house 61:* «**Admodum R[everen]dus Dominus JOSEPH DEPRATO, ex Parochus Cerovgl[ie], Jubilatus, ex Loco Gallogor.** · ann[orum] **80** · Senect[us]»

***A retired parish priest of Cerovlje, living at Gologorica, dead at eighty — so born about 1721.*** *He is the man in this book's officiant column as* «D. JOSEPH: DEPRATO, ex Paroch[us]», *and he heads its index block* «Deprato Leonardus N.º 6». *[The archive has twice had to pull this family apart from ours](/gologorica-line/); it can now do it with a date.* *(doc.)*

**⚠ AND THE PARISH PRIEST'S HAND STOPS TWO YEARS BEFORE HE DIES.** *Through 1795 the officiant column reads* «**Defranc[eschi]** P[res]b[yte]r Loci». *From 22 November 1797 it reads* «**Felix Ant. Babich** P[res]b[yte]r Loci» *and never goes back.* ***The handover is explained by an entry this archive already holds***: *[Mathias de Franceschi, former parish priest of Gallignana, died 29 March 1798 of* **«Paralisia»***](/gologorica-line/).* **A stroke takes the pen out of his hand about two years before it takes his life, and the register shows the gap.**

**Two epidemics, back to back, and the book lets you count them.** *1789 —* **«Pustulla»**, *smallpox: beyond [the two Defranceschi children already published](/gologorica-line/), six more between September and November, aged three months to thirty, at houses 74, 13, 11, 24, 9 and 90. Then* **1790 — «Fluxus»**, *dysentery, which takes almost the whole of page 10 through that August;* ***house 102 buries three in seven weeks.*** *Smallpox returns in 1797–98.*

**⭐ AND THE CAUSE-OF-DEATH COLUMN SOMETIMES SAYS SOMETHING A PARISH REGISTER IS NOT SUPPOSED TO SAY.**

*1797, a man of 68, in service since boyhood:* «**Egestas**» — *destitution.* *1803, a woman of 70 at house 100:* «**Fames**» — ***hunger.*** *The same year, a man of 67:* «Egestas» *again. And in January 1795, a boy who lived* **two hours**, *at house 62:* «**Ignorantia obstetricis**» — ***the midwife's ignorance.*** *A priest filling in a printed column, naming poverty and blame where the form asked only for a disease.*
*Pages 1–22 are now* **walked**, *not sampled. The remaining frames of this book are not, and [the worklist says so](/worklist/).*

deathwalk2.heading: Pages 23 to 28 — a hunger year, the Deprato collision made real, and a page that is unreadable on the frame that shows it
deathwalk2.lead: *The walk continued through 1803–1805.* **Still no Defranceschi death** *— and three things that change how this archive reads the rest of the film.*
paras:
**⭐ FIRST, AND IT IS A WARNING ABOUT METHOD RATHER THAN A FACT ABOUT A FAMILY: this film shoots some pages twice, and the duplicate can be the only one you can read.**

*Page 28 is on* **M01069241** *and again on* **M01069242**. *On the first, a* **loose slip of paper lies across the page** *and blanks out* ***seven entries***. *On the second the slip has been lifted away and they are all there.* *The two exposures share their top two entries exactly, which is how the pages are known to be the same page.* ***A session that read M01069241 and moved on would have recorded page 28 as read and lost seven deaths.***

**And what the slip was hiding is a household coming apart in fourteen weeks.** *House 28, 1805:*

> **20 April** — «Johanna Peer **nata Luxetich**, uxor Johanis · ann 34 · **Parthus**» *— dead in childbirth, aged thirty-four.*
> **7 May** — «Johanes Peer, fil. Joh: · ann 6 · Vermes» *— her six-year-old.*
> **30 July** — «Cath: … da Peer, filia Joh: · **mens. 3** · Debilitas» *— a three-month-old, so born about the week her mother died.*

***The birth that killed the mother, the child it produced, and a brother in between.*** *(doc.)*

**⚠ AND THE SLIP ITSELF IS A RECORD, of a kind this book is not supposed to contain.** *It is in Italian:* «**Fieni parochiali venduto all'ast[a]** per il prezzo che segue» — ***parish hay sold at auction***, *three buyers:* «Pietro Basilisco · f 37:60», «Giovanni Marcich · f 40:50», «**Alberto D.r Peschle** · f 13:3», *together* **f 91:13**. *[The Peschle are a family this archive already follows](/married-in/) — Dr Albertus Peschle, physician, kept Gologorica house 2 and stood godfather to a Defranceschi child in 1869.* **⚠ But the slip is LOOSE and carries no date of its own, and a loose slip takes no date from the page it happens to be lying on.** *It is recorded as* ***undated***, *and whether this Alberto is that Dr Albertus is [a question, not a finding](/worklist/).*

**⭐ SECOND — the Defranceschi/Deprato collision, which this archive has twice described as a hazard, actually happens on page 24.**

> «61. · **13 Xmbris** [1803] · **Catharina DEPRATO** nata Rovisi **ex Petin**, **uxor Joh: Baptista** · ann **43** · Hidrope»

*Set that beside an entry already published here:* «**Catharina DEFRANCESCHI** nata Jablich, **uxor Joannis Baptistæ**, house 36, **1792**, ann 26, Apoplexia». ***Two women, each «Catharina, wife of Joannes Baptista», eleven years apart in the same book.*** *The index files them under two different households —* «Defranceschi Joseph N.º 17» *and* «Deprato Leonardus N.º 6» *— and house 61 is where [the retired priest Joseph Deprato](/gologorica-line/) had died two years earlier.* **Only the surname and the house number tell them apart. [The rule that keeps them apart earned its keep again.](/method/)**

**THIRD — 1803 was a hunger year, and the priest wrote it in the cause column five times.** *Beyond the* «Fames» *already published:* «**Cancrhrena famesque**» *(gangrene and hunger, a woman of 56),* «**Egestas**» *for a woman of 64, and —* ***the hardest line on the page*** — *house 6, 31 October:* «Mattia Zabran … nata Ghersan, **inventa mortua domi** · ann 32 · **Egestas**». ***Found dead in her own house, aged thirty-two, of destitution.***

vetusnovus.heading: The register stops inferring and says it: «36 vetus · 14 novus»
vetusnovus.lead: **On page 30 the house-number column splits in two, and the priest labels the halves.** *This archive had [worked the renumbering out by inference](/worklist/) from two unlabelled columns in the baptism register and left it open, with the right test written down:* «a consistent bijection is a renumbering; a scatter is error». ***The death register settles the first half of that question in its own words.***
paras:
**⭐ AND THE LINE THAT CARRIES THE LABELS IS A DEFRANCESCHI DEATH.**

> «Idem Parochus · **36 vetus** · **14 novus** · die **12 8bris 1806** · **Catharina filia defti Josephi De=franceschi, CÆLEBS ex Loco** · **56** ann. · **Asthma**»

***[Catharina Defranceschi](/person/catharina-defranceschi-d1806/), daughter of a Josephus already dead, unmarried, fifty-six, of asthma*** *— so born about 1750. She was found where the priest filed her: the book's own index lists* «Catharina filia q. Josephi — 30». *(doc.)*

*She is the* **second** *unmarried Defranceschi woman in this book, after [Sancta, «cælebs», fifty-eight, in 1792](/person/sancta-defranceschi-d1792/).* **⚠ Her birth year is not declared**: *fifty-six in 1806 implies 1750, and [an implied year is not a declared one](/method/).*

**Why the two words matter more than the one death.** *[This archive identifies its two eighteenth-century households as* **«casa 31»** *and* **«casa 36»***](/gologorica-line/), *and it has already warned itself that* ***a casa number in one book is not the same house in another***. **Here is casa 36 bridged in a single line: «36 vetus · 14 novus».** *Not inferred — written.*

**⚠ BUT THE SAME PAGE BREAKS THE PATTERN THE ARCHIVE HAD GUESSED AT, and that is the honest headline.**

*The earlier reading noted the second column running* «almost always about half» *the first —* 9→4, 38→19, 42→21, 54→27, 72→36, 112→69. *The labelled pairs on page 30 do not behave like that at all:*

| vetus | novus |
|---|---|
| **36** | **14** |
| **8** | **52** |
| **107** | **76** |
| 70 | 8? *(uncertain)* |

***«8 vetus» becomes «52 novus» — six times larger, not half.*** **So these are a permutation, not a scaling**, *which is what renumbering a village by walking a different route actually produces.* **⚠ It also means the two column-pairs may not be the same mapping at all**, *and the «about half» reading is now* ***unsettled rather than confirmed***. *Nothing earlier is withdrawn; [the question goes back to the worklist with three solid pairs attached](/worklist/), which is three more than it had.*
*The table is extended as the walk goes on, exactly as [the worklist asked](/worklist/). Four pairs is not a concordance. It is the start of one.*

deathwalk3.heading: Pages 31 to 36 — who paid for the bells, who was buried «gratis», and a sixth priest from Krbune
deathwalk3.lead: *1807 to 1812.* **No Defranceschi dies in these six pages** *— another named nil. But read together with the flyleaf, they make the parish's* ***economy of death*** *legible, which is not something this archive could do yesterday.*
paras:
**⭐ THREE LEDGERS IN ONE BOOK, and they answer each other.**

*On the flyleaf, five families* **pay** *a ducat for [the ringing of all three bells](/gologorica-line/). In the register, 1803, people die of* «**Fames**» *and* «**Egestas**» *— hunger and destitution. And on page 35, in 1811, the priest writes a single word under his own name on three consecutive burials:*

> «**gratis**»

***The burial was free.*** *Houses 83, 34 and 93.* **So the same book records who could pay for bells, who paid nothing at all, and who starved** *— and no Defranceschi appears in any of the three lists.*

**⭐ «Joannes Baptista DEPRATO, Viduus» — and the Deprato house moves number, which may be the renumbering again.**

> *p. 32:* «6. · die 30ma Martii **1809** · **Joannes Baptista Deprato, Viduus** · **56** · Inflammatio et Tussis»

*He is a* **widower**, *and [this archive now holds his wife](/gologorica-line/):* «Catharina Deprato … **uxor Joh: Baptista**», *dead* **13 December 1803** *— at house* **61**. *He dies at house* **6**. **⚠ The 1803 entry predates the «vetus/novus» labelling and the 1809 entry follows it, so the obvious reading is that house 61 old became house 6 new.** *That would also agree with [the 1826 census, which puts DEPRATO at house 6](/gologorica-line/).* ***It is an inference, not a labelled pair, and it is recorded as one*** *— [the concordance only counts what the priest actually wrote](/worklist/).*

**A SIXTH PRIEST FROM KRBUNE, and this time the arrangement is spelled out.** *p. 33, 1809:* «R.dus D.nus **Ant: Trinaistich** … **Cherbunensis**, ***de Licentia mea*** Parochus» — *by my licence.* *[Worklist 168](/worklist/) was raised because an archpriest of «Cherbune» stood godfather to a Defranceschi child in 1785, and has collected sightings ever since.* **This is the sixth, and with [the 1805 interregnum](/gologorica-line/) it is now clear the two parishes lent each other clergy as a standing arrangement, not an accident.**

**The village had strangers in it.** *p. 33, 9 June 1809, house 1:* «**Gertrudis Zwey, Vidua, ex HYPERLABACO**» — ***a widow from Oberlaibach***, *which is Vrhnika above Ljubljana — dead at forty-six, with a long marginal note of absolution signed by the administrator of Cerovlje.* *A German surname, a Carniolan town, and a parish register that normally runs on twenty local families.*

**And two human details the columns were not designed to hold.** *p. 32, 1808, a six-hour-old girl:* «**fuit ab obstetrice baptizata** ob necessitatem et periculum in mora» — ***baptised by the midwife***, *for necessity and the danger in delay. Thirteen years after the same column had blamed [a midwife's ignorance for a death](/gologorica-line/).* *And p. 36, 1 January 1812, house 9:* «Joannes Peer defti Joannis **filius POSTHUMUS**», *two months old —* ***a son born after his father was buried***, *and the father is on page 36 too, dead of phthisis the previous August at forty-three.*

**The book is also being inspected.** «Revisus in Visitatione Decanali die 11a 7mbris **1807**», «Revisus et approbatus … die 25 Junii **1808**» *— both signed* **Petrus Anicich, Cæs. Reg.us Parochus et Decanus** *— and again* «die 5 Julii **1816** In Visitatione decanali». *With [the 1805 note](/gologorica-line/) that is four decanal visitations in eleven years, which is a layer of administration above the parish this archive had not seen.*

fames1815.heading: 1815–1816 — thirteen months of hunger, counted entry by entry
fames1815.lead: **Page 41 carries three deaths from want in eleven weeks, and the last of them is not a death at Gologorica at all.** *It is the parish recording one of its own who* ***left***, *and why, and where he was buried — with a certificate from the priest who buried him.*
paras:
> **27 April 1815, house 80**
> *name:* «**Joannes Ancich q.m Judicis Joannis filius ex Rismagnizza**»
> *age:* «annor. **40**» *· cause:* «**FAMES**»
> *when:* «obiit in Istria ex Veneto, quo ***egestatis causa cum familia sua se contulerat***»
> *who buried him:* «Adm. R.dus D.nus **Matthæus Loganis, Parochus Foscolini in Istria ex Veneta**, sepelivit ibi in **Ecclesia S.ti Rochi**, *uti ex ejusdem Parochi Attestato patet*»

***He died in Venetian Istria, where he had taken himself and his family for reason of destitution.*** *Buried in the church of St Roch by the parish priest of Foscolino, and entered here on the strength of that priest's written certificate.* **And he was the son of the «Judex» — the village judge.** *Not a landless man. [The office appears elsewhere in this book](/gologorica-line/), on Andreas Cancianich in 1800 and on Martinus Zabran in 1808.* ***The headman's son starved at forty, in another country.*** *(doc.)*

**⚠ Two things this archive is NOT claiming.** *Where* «Foscolino in Istria ex Veneta» *is today —* **not identified here**, *and guessed at nowhere.* *And why 1815 was a hunger year is* **not** *explained: Tambora erupted that April and the famous failed summer was 1816, but this man was already dead on 27 April 1815, so whatever emptied his house happened before that. [The register states the fact; the cause is somebody else's research.](/worklist/)*

**He is the third on one page.** *12 February — a stranger* «**ex Parochia Paasbergensi**», *about forty,* «**inventus mortuus in via in Doll**» — ***found dead on the road***. *6 March, house 54, at eight at night —* «Matthæus Flegar alias Sidre … **Inopia consumptus**», ***consumed by want***, *at fifty-four.*

**Set beside [1803](/gologorica-line/), this is the parish's second hunger crisis in twelve years** — *and the second time its priest reached past the printed column for a word that means poverty rather than disease.* **⚠ No Defranceschi is among them**, *on this page or on any page of the walk so far. The family that this archive follows was not in the lists of those who paid for bells, nor those buried* «gratis», *nor those who starved.* ***That is four kinds of absence, and all four are now documented rather than assumed.***

**⭐ AND THE WALK KEPT GOING, SO THE COUNT GOT WORSE. What page 41 shows in eleven weeks runs for thirteen months.**

*Pages 42 to 44, read after the above was first written:*

| when | who | age | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 Mar 1815 | Matthæus Flegar, h.54 | 54 | «Inopia consumptus» |
| **27 Apr 1815** | **Joannes Ancich**, h.80 | **40** | «**Fames**» *— in Venetian Istria* |
| 11 May 1815 | Catharina ux. Jacobi **Ancich**, h.79 | 46 | «**Fames**» |
| 28 May 1815 | Joannes Udovicich, h.92 | 52 | «**Fames** et paralysis» |
| 1 Feb 1816 | Joanas Zabran, h.46 | 45 | «**Tabes famelica**» |
| **1 Apr 1816** | **Lucia Rabar**, h.84 | **4** | «**Fames**» |
| 16 Apr 1816 | Joanes Bapta Udovicich, h.75 | 58 | «Tussis et **Fames**» |

***Seven deaths the priest attributed to hunger, across thirteen months*** *— and [with the five of 1803](/gologorica-line/) that is* **twelve** *in this book, written in a column printed for diseases.* **The youngest is four years and five months old.**

**⚠ And it is not the poorest houses alone.** *The man who died in Venetian Istria was the son of the* **«Judex»**, *the village judge. The woman at the foot of page 44 is the wife of the* **«Suppanus»** *— the župan, the headman.* ***Two of the village's officeholding families are inside the casualty list.*** *Whatever this was, it did not stop at the bottom of the parish.*

**The Ancich of houses 79 to 81 are hit hardest of all** — *four deaths in 1815: Joannes at forty in another country, Catharina at forty-six of hunger, Mathia at sixty-five, and Joannes the widower at seventy-two, who had to be* «sepultus … ***ob signa putrefactionis***» *— buried the next morning because the body had already begun to go.*

famine1817.heading: The famine of 1817 — fifty-two deaths and still counting, off a register nobody had read
famine1817.lead:
**Page 51 of the death book carries seven burials between 26 April and 8 May 1817. The cause column reads the same for every one of them.**

> «**Fames**»

*Hunger. [The earlier write-up of this crisis](/gologorica-line/) counted seven deaths over thirteen months and said so. Walking on to page 51 shows that was the beginning of it.*
paras:
**⭐ THE COUNT, and it is made by reading every entry rather than by sampling.**

| period | hunger-attributed deaths |
|---|---|
| **1803** | **5** |
| **1815** *(Mar–May)* | **4** |
| **1816** | **3** |
| **1817** *(Jan–May alone)* | **22** |
| | ***at least 34*** |

*The words the priest used:* «**Fames**» *(hunger),* «**Egestas**» *(destitution),* «**Inopia consumptus**» *(consumed by want),* «**Tabes famelica**» *(famine wasting),* «**Cancrhrena famesque**», «**Extenuatio**», *and* «**Debilitates fame mendicando**». ***Seven different constructions, in a column printed for diseases.*** **⚠ The walk stopped at page 51 with the deaths still running**, *so* ***34 is a floor, not a total***, *and [the worklist says so](/worklist/).*

**⭐ THE COUNT, revised upward as the walk went on — which is why it is given as a floor and not a total.**

| period | hunger-attributed deaths |
|---|---|
| **1803** | **5** |
| **1815** *(Mar–May)* | **4** |
| **1816** | **3** |
| **1817** *(Jan–Jul)* | ***about 40*** |
| **running total** | ***at least 52*** |

*An earlier version of this section said* «at least 34» *after reading to page 51.* **Pages 52 to 54 added eighteen more, so the figure was raised rather than defended.** ***The walk stopped at page 54 with the deaths still running at a dozen a month, so 52 remains a floor.*** *[The worklist carries the unfinished part.](/worklist/)*

*The words the priest reached for:* «**Fames**», «**Egestas**», «**Inopia consumptus**», «**Tabes famelica**», «**Hydropisis famelica**», «**Cancrhrena famesque**», «**Extenuatio**», «**Fluxus sanguinis et Fames**», *and* «**Debilitates fame mendicando**». ***Nine constructions, in a column printed for diseases.***

**⭐ AND IT RAN THROUGH WHOLE HOUSEHOLDS.** *The youngest are* **one year old**; *the roll runs* **1, 1, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 20**.

· **House 81, the Rabar «haeredis Ancich» — FOUR**: *Lucia,* **4** *(Apr 1816); Anna,* **3** *(Jan 1817); Joanna,* **7** *(May 1817); and on 18 May their father* **Georgius, 40**, «Fames et hydropisis».
· **House 46, the Zabran Schina — FOUR**: *the father, «Tabes famelica», Feb 1816; Maria,* **5**; *Josephus,* **18**, «inventus mortuus ruri» *and buried only* «post sectionem **a chirurgo** factam»; *Joannes,* **16**.
· **House 105, the Rade «alias Picin» — THREE**: *Antonius,* **39**, *found at daybreak* «sub dio **in abysso**»; *Helena,* **3**; *Joannes,* **8**.
· **House 73, the Udovicich «alias Scloch» — two brothers five days apart**, **6** *and* **7**.
· **House 75, the Udovicich Giacotich — THREE**: *father* **58**, *daughter* **14**, *mother* **55** *(«hydropisis famelica»).*
· **House 117, the Pelesco — THREE**: **9**, **55**, **11**.

**The register also records what people did to survive, which a parish register is not designed to hold.**

· **They begged.** *25 April 1817, house 19:* «Joannes Batta Crismarich … **Debilitates fame mendicando**, Pleuritide obiit» — ***weakened by hunger while begging.***
· **They left.** *[27 April 1815 — Venetian Istria,](/gologorica-line/)* «egestatis causa cum familia sua se contulerat». *1 April 1817 — Maria Schina* «obiit **Paalbergæ**», *buried by the Paasberg parish priest.* *Both entered here on the receiving priest's written word.*
· **They died where they fell.** «inventus mortuus **in via**» *(1815),* «inventus moribundus **sub dio in abysso**» *(1817),* «inventus mortuus **ruri**» *(1817),* «**inventa mortua**» *(1817).*

**⚠ WHAT THIS ARCHIVE IS AND IS NOT SAYING ABOUT THE CAUSE.** *The peak —* **22 deaths in the first five months of 1817** *— falls exactly where the post-Tambora failed harvest of 1816 would put it, and the European famine of 1816–17 is well known.* **But the register proves a famine at Gologorica; it does not prove its cause**, *and [the 1815 deaths are a separate and earlier phase](/gologorica-line/) that cannot be Tambora at all — Joannes Ancich was already dead on 27 April 1815, eleven days after the eruption and long before any harvest could fail.* ***Two phases, one of which the famous explanation does not fit.*** *Stated, not explained.*

**⚠ AND THE REASON THIS SITS ON A DEFRANCESCHI PAGE: no Defranceschi is in any of it.** *Across [pages 1 to 51, every entry read](/searched/), the family appears* **five times** *and never once among the hunger dead, never among the five households that paid for [the ringing of all three bells](/gologorica-line/), and never among the burials marked* «gratis». ***An absence across fifty-one walked pages is not silence. It is a finding, and it is the kind this archive exists to make.***

**⭐ AND THE WALK FOUND THE SHAPE OF THE WHOLE CRISIS, which one page could never have shown.**

| months | what the cause column says |
|---|---|
| **Jan – Jul 1817** | «**Fames**» *and its eight cousins — about 40 deaths* |
| **Aug – Sep 1817** | «**Fluxus**», «Dissenteria seu **Fluxus sanguinis violentus**» — ***dysentery*** |
| **Oct – Dec 1817** | «Febris maligna», «Phtysis», «Asthma» — *the long tail* |

***Starvation first, then the epidemic that takes the starved.*** *By page 63 the register is back to ordinary mortality — and the form itself has changed, now recording the dead person's* «conditio» *(«rusticus», «rustica») and carrying the parish priest's signature.*

**Three small things the walk picked up that no index would have.**

· *A girl of ten on page 55 is entered as* «**muta et surda**» — ***deaf and mute***, *the only disability named anywhere in the walk.*
· *Burials begin to be ordered the same day* «ob signa putrefactionis, **et nimium foetorem**» *— in a hot summer with more dead than the parish could keep up with.*
· *And a death on 2 July is entered among the* **September** *burials, with the priest explaining himself:* «**Hic inscriptus, quia mense 7bri demum mors ejusdem scripto tenus ab eodem Parocho annunciata fuit**» — *entered here because only in September was the death announced in writing.* ***It is a sixteen-year-old, dead of «Fames» at San Pietro in Selve*** — *the fourth of this parish's people to die away from home in the crisis.*

**⚠ One note for whoever films or orders this reel next.** *A conservation label is photographed with page 56:* «**WATER DAMAGE · OŠTEĆENO OD VLAGE**». *The archive at Pazin has flagged damp damage at this point in the volume, and [this archive records that rather than discovering it twice](/method/).*

indexhouses.heading: The death book's index is not a list of names — it is a directory of houses
indexhouses.lead: *Every Defranceschi block in the index is headed with a name and a* «**N.º**» — «Joseph N.º 17», «Joanes Bapta detti Lonardi N.º 12», «Leonardus N.º 10», *and beside them* «Deprato Leonardus N.º 6». **The walk has now read enough of the pages those blocks point at to say what the number is.**
paras:
**⭐ IT IS THE HOUSE NUMBER. Five tests, five matches — and the two that fail, fail for a reason.**

| index block | house in the register | |
|---|---|---|
| «**Deprato** Leonardus **N.º 6**» | J. B. Deprato d. 1809 · Catharina vid. Leonardi Deprato d. 1817 · the 1826 census — ***all house 6*** | ✔✔✔ |
| «Defranceschi **Joseph N.º 17**» | Amalia filia Josephi, d. 1826, ***house 17*** | ✔ |
| «Defranceschi **Joanes Bapta detti Lonardi N.º 12**» | Maria filia defti Joan: Baptæ, d. 1826, ***house 12*** | ✔ |
| «Defranceschi **Leonardus N.º 10**» | Antonius «Leonardi pater», d. **1802**, house **29** | ✘ |
| *(Joseph's block)* Catharina, d. **1806** | «36 **vetus** · 14 **novus**» | ✘ |

***The two failures are both from before or during [the renumbering](/gologorica-line/).*** **So the index gives each household's house in the NEW numbering, assigned once when the index was compiled** *— not the house as it stood at each death.* *That is why a 1802 entry and a 1826 entry under the same heading can carry different numbers and neither be wrong.*

**⭐ WHICH MEANS THIS ARCHIVE NOW HAS ADDRESSES FOR ITS THREE EIGHTEENTH-CENTURY DEFRANCESCHI HOUSEHOLDS**, *in the numbering the 1826 census and every later register uses:*

> **Joseph — house 17** · **Joannes Baptista «detti Lonardi» — house 12** · **Leonardus — house 10**

*and, next door and not ours,* **Deprato Leonardus — house 6**.

**⚠ AND IT YIELDS A PREDICTION THE CONCORDANCE CAN BE TESTED AGAINST.** *If «Leonardus N.º 10» is house 10 new, and the one man the index files under him —* [Antonius, «Leonardi pater»](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/) *— died at house* **29** *in 1802, in the old numbering, then* ***29 vetus should equal 10 novus***. **⚠ That is a hypothesis, not a pair**: *it is not written in the book the way [«36 vetus · 14 novus» is](/gologorica-line/), and [the concordance counts only what the priest wrote](/worklist/).* ***It is offered as something the next pages can confirm or kill.***

**And the entry that completed the table is itself worth having.** *Page 66, 30 September 1826, house 12:* «**Maria filia Defti Jo:is B:tæ Defranceschi** · 37 · **hectica**», *and then the part no census could hold —* «**Ca[pell]anus ad S. Petrum in Barbana, ibi sepelivit**». *[This archive already knew she died that day](/person/maria-rosalia-defranceschi-1789/), from the 1826 household census, which gives her age to the day and fixes her birth at 20 July 1789.* ***What was new is that she was buried at Barban, forty kilometres south, and not in her own parish.*** **⚠ Why she was there is not known, and is not guessed at here.**

twosystems.heading: Two numbering systems, not one — which is why the renumbering would not come out
twosystems.lead: **From 1830 the death register writes the house as a fraction.** *Five of them on page 71:* **65/32 · 103/61 · 41/17 · 111/68 · 31/12**. *The upper number runs between* **1.6 and 2.6 times** *the lower.*
paras:
**⭐ AND THAT IS THE «ABOUT HALF» PATTERN — which means it is NOT the pairing the 1806 entries label.**

*[This archive had noticed two unlabelled columns in the* **baptism** *register](/worklist/) running* «almost always about half» — 9→4, 38→19, 42→21, 54→27, 72→36, 112→69. *And [earlier in this walk the* **death** *register labelled a different pair outright](/gologorica-line/):* «36 **vetus** · 14 **novus**», «8 vetus · 52 novus», «107 vetus · 76 novus» — ***which scatter, and one of which more than sextuples.***

| | relation | labelled? |
|---|---|---|
| **1806 pairs** | ***scatter*** — 36→14, 8→52, 107→76 | **yes** — «vetus» / «novus» |
| **1830s fractions** | ***consistently ~2×*** — 65/32, 41/17, 31/12 | **no** |

***These are two different things, and worklist 171 has been asking about them as though they were one.*** **That is why the table would not come out.**

**⚠ WHAT IS NOW SETTLED AND WHAT IS NOT.**

**Settled:** *the village* **was** *renumbered about 1806 — the priest says so in his own words. Three labelled pairs stand: 36→14, 8→52, 107→76.*

**Not settled, and not guessed at here:** ***what the 1830s fraction is***. *It behaves like a ratio, not a permutation, which is the signature of something other than a renumbering —* **a conscription number, a cadastral parcel, or houses grouped in pairs would all do that.** *Which number is the house and which is the other thing is* **not** *established, because unlike the 1806 entries* ***nobody labelled these***.

**⚠ AND ONE PAIR IS WORTH A SECOND LOOK, as a lead and not a finding.** *The fifth fraction on the page is* **31/12**. *[This archive's two eighteenth-century Defranceschi households are](/gologorica-line/)* «**casa 31**» *and* «casa 36», *and [the baptism book's own index bridges](/gologorica-line/)* «Defranceschi Joanes Bapta **detti Leonardi** · N.º **12**» *— the same 31 and the same 12.* **⚠ But the 1831 entry at 31/12 is a CRISMANICH**, *not a Defranceschi, and [Maria Defranceschi died at house 12 only five years earlier](/person/maria-rosalia-defranceschi-1789/).* ***So either houses changed hands, or the fraction does not mean what it looks like.*** *It is recorded as a coincidence worth testing, not as a bridge. [The worklist carries it.](/worklist/)*

**⭐ THE TABLE, COLLECTED — nineteen pairs, and it answers the test the worklist set itself.**

*From the death register, pages 71–73 (1830–33), and the six already held from [the baptism register](/worklist/):*

> 9/4 · 31/12 · 38/19 · 41/17 · 42/21 · 54/27 · 55/25 · 57/36 · 61/29 · 64/31 · 65/32 · 72/36 · 80/43 · 85/44 · 92/50 · 94/52 · 103/61 · 111/68 · 112/69

**⭐⭐ AND TWO OF THEM — 72/36 and 112/69 — ARE EXACTLY PAIRS FROM THE BAPTISM REGISTER'S TABLE.** ***So the baptism book and the death book are using the same pairing.*** *That is worth having: it means the evidence from the two books can be pooled, which it could not be while they were separate puzzles.*

**What the nineteen pairs actually show, stated flatly:**

| | |
|---|---|
| upper numbers run | **9 – 112** |
| lower numbers run | **4 – 69** |
| ratio | **1.58 – 2.58**, clustered near **2** |
| order-preserving? | ***no*** |

***The two series are of different sizes***, *which a plain renumbering would not produce — a renumbering moves the labels and keeps the count.* **And it is not even monotone**: *41/17 crosses 38/19, and 55/25 crosses 54/27, so the mapping shuffles locally as well as compressing.*

**⚠ SO THE HONEST POSITION, and it is better than the one this item started with.**

**Established:** *a single consistent pairing, used in* **both** *registers, between a series running past 110 and a series stopping near 70; near-2:1; not order-preserving; and* ***distinct from the labelled 1806 renumbering***.

**Not established, and deliberately not guessed:** ***what the lower series is***. *A conscription number, a cadastral parcel, a tax unit or a hamlet-level numbering would each fit a smaller series paired to the houses. [This archive will not name it without a document that names it.](/method/)*

**⚠ And two readings in the table above are this session's and uncertain —** *57/36 and 103/61 were taken at page scale. They are flagged rather than dropped, because [a table nobody can audit is worse than a short one](/method/).*

civis1848.heading: «Civis», not «agricola» — and a child named for a man who had fifteen months left
civis1848.lead:
*Page 84 of the death book, under 1848, in a column of farmers:*

> «**Aprilis 14°** · **5** · **Leonardus Defranceschi, CIVIS**, refectus SS Sacramentis moribundorum et sepultus die 15° hujus · **82** · febris cum senectute»
paras: **⚠ FIRST, WHAT IS NOT NEW: [the archive already had this death](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1766/), to the day.** *@I20@ has carried* **born 30 January 1766, died 14 April 1848** *for some time. Finding the entry is a* ***verification***. **But the roster row carried those two years and NOTHING ELSE — not a note, not a citation.** *[The third such row found in one afternoon.](/method/)*

**What the entry adds.** *The house —* **5** *— the cause, the burial on the following day, the last rites received, and one word that does a great deal of work:*

> «**CIVIS**»

***Every other adult on that page is «agricola», a farmer.*** *He is a* **burgher**. *[The same distinction follows this family through the registers](/gologorica-line/) — it is why the 1826 census enters them as* cives, *why [Dr Albertus Peschle married into them](/married-in/), and why their sons appear as students, a painter and an army doctor while the village around them works the ground.* **And the arithmetic closes**: *eighty-two in April 1848 lands on the birth already held, 30 January 1766.*

**⭐ AND THE THING THE TWO BOOKS SAY TOGETHER, which neither says alone.**

*On* **22 January 1847**, *at* **house 5**, *[a boy was baptised* **Leonardus Defranceschi**](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1847/). *On* **14 April 1848**, *at* **house 5**, ***Leonardus Defranceschi died at eighty-two***.

**Fifteen months.** *The child was not named for a dead grandfather, the usual pattern in these books — [he was named for a living one](/namesakes/), and the old man had over a year to be called by his own name in the same house.* *The boy lived until 1917, and [his death is written into the margin of his own baptism seventy years later](/gologorica-line/).*

**And two children on the same page who had no family at all.** *8 August 1848, house 46:* «**Emilia Emerling, ex expositis**», *aged one. 10 December, house 23:* «Antonius Vincentius …, **ex expositis**», *nine months.* ***«Ex expositis» — from among the exposed: foundlings, boarded out from a city hospital to village families who were paid to keep them.*** **⚠ Neither surname is local**, *which is the usual mark of the traffic. This archive had not seen it in these registers before, and records it as a* ***category to watch***, *not as a finding about anybody's line.*

dupframes.heading: Twice now, the duplicate frame has been the only one you can read
dupframes.lead: **This reel photographs some openings twice, and [the archive's own coverage check says two attempts to detect that automatically FAILED](/method/).** *Walking the book has now found two pairs by eye — and in* ***both*** *cases the first exposure was the defective one.*
paras:
| opening | first exposure | second exposure |
|---|---|---|
| **pages 27–28** *(1805)* | **M01069241** — *a loose slip of paper lies across the page and* ***blanks out seven entries*** | **M01069242** — *slip lifted away, all present* |
| **pages 81–82** *(1845–46)* | **M01069269** — *the left edge is cut off and* ***the month column goes with it*** | **M01069270** — *framed wider, months legible* |

***On the first, page 82 gives seven deaths dated 22, 4, 26, 8, 28, 12, 26 — with no month attached to any of them.*** *On the second they are Martii 22, Augusti 4, 8bris 26, 9bris 8, 9bris 28, Decembris 12, Decembris 26.* **A whole year's worth of dates that exist only on the duplicate.**

**⚠ SO THE WORKING RULE, and it is cheap to follow:** ***before accepting a page as read, look at the frame on either side of it.*** *It costs two seconds and it has twice been the difference between a page recorded as read and a page actually read.*

**⚠ And it means the frame counts overstate the book.** *[The coverage figure](/method/) counts* **frames cited**, *and two of the frames counted here are one opening. The true number of distinct pages read is lower than the frame count says, by an amount nobody can yet state —* ***which is recorded rather than quietly corrected.***
*Both pairs were found by walking. Neither would have been found by going to a page the index pointed at and stopping there.*
